Stored summary bytes are now immutable evidence. Post-hoc reduction writes a new, non-clobbering artifact (including the repaired anchor envelope) or refuses; the raw-artifact immutability and pure-reducer portions of D-002/D-028 remain in force. Frozen 0.5.0/0.6.0 numeric semantics remain replayable and are not claim-bearing merely because they can be read.</p> <h3>D-078 additive registry addendum — 2026-07-20: causal-set repair</h3> <p>The closed registry additionally includes floor/whole-window barriers <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code>, <code>whole_window_verdict_coverage_incomplete</code>, <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code>, and <code>whole_window_verdict_conflict</code>. Instrument-evidence diagnostics additionally include <code>no_plateau_interior_intervals</code>, <code>plateau_below_minimum</code>, <code>robust_snr_below_minimum</code>, <code>edge_coverage_missing</code>, <code>model_fit_not_significant</code>, and <code>fitted_shift_exceeds_validation_limit</code>. These additions only refuse or widen uncertainty; none can license a claim.</p> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-21: convergence fix wave (lead adjudications)</h3> <p>Recorded by the lead after the two-round cross-model convergence loop over <code>impl/p0-instrument-repair</code> (round-2 and round-3 fix waves; council log carries the layer accounting). Six rulings:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Additive causal-bound composition.</strong> <code>B_effective = B_bundle + B_fiducial</code> replaces <code>max(B_bundle, B_fiducial)</code>. The bundle-local censored-constraint anchor interval and the instrument&#39;s emission-lag bound sit on disjoint causal links; no containment proof exists, so <code>max()</code> under-composes. <code>B_fiducial</code> itself additively folds in the calibration capture&#39;s own trace-anchor bound. The prior <code>max()</code> text in this log is superseded prospectively; stored summaries are never rewritten.</li> <li><strong>Identity bump, not in-place semantics change.</strong> The additive composition, fiducial protocol_v2 physics (<code>joint_loss_sublevel_interval_branch_v2</code> full 2-D branch-and-bound region), and the stricter evidence-admission semantics are minted as reducer <code>0.5.2</code> / AXI <code>0.6.2</code> with <code>configs/calibration/powermetrics_fiducial/protocol_v2.json</code>. <code>0.5.1</code> / <code>0.6.1</code> and <code>protocol_v1.json</code> remain byte-frozen replay arms.</li> <li><strong>Superseded arms are claim-ineligible.</strong> <code>0.5.1</code>/<code>0.6.1</code> summaries refuse claim-bearing use with a registered refusal (superseded max-composition envelope semantics); <code>0.5.2</code>/<code>0.6.2</code> are the sole claim-eligible mints.</li> <li><strong>Registry additions (closing the F11/PENDING exception).</strong> The closed refusal vocabulary additionally includes <code>token_count_stream_chunk_fallback</code> (renamed from the source-label reuse of <code>stream_chunk_fallback</code>), <code>pulse_calibration_rollover_gate_timeout</code> (pre-workload rollover gate timeout now refuses fail-closed, no artifact minting), and <code>post_window_trace_tail_shorter_than_anchor_bound</code> (reduce-time refusal when the post-window trace tail cannot support the composed anchor bound; collection policy raises the minimum post-window dwell to 1.0 s). These only refuse; none can license a claim.</li> <li><strong>Registry closure is one-way by design.</strong> Every emitted spelling must be registered here; a registered spelling with no current emission site (e.g. <code>window_evidence_precheck_failed</code>, <code>cap_hit_drift_term_unavailable</code>) is permitted — unemittable names cannot launder anything.</li> <li><strong>Member-level <code>claim_evidence_flags</code> is an all-leaf union — documented, not changed.</strong> Adjudicated a documentation defect only: the union is fail-safe (it can only over-flag, never over-admit) and gating decisions read the per-metric leaves. Scope documented in <code>docs/contracts/run_bundle_layout.md</code>; no wire rename.</li> </ol> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-21 (second): two-edge envelope and confirmation-round rulings</h3> <p>Recorded by the lead after the first confirmation round over <code>5093355</code> correctly withheld sign-off (fresh Sol xhigh audit; 8 confirmed findings, one P0). Rulings:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Corner-composed two-edge envelope (P0 repair).</strong> The calibration fits independent start-edge and stop-edge emission lags; a single common trace shift under-covers because independent endpoint errors move energy by up to <code>2·P·B_fiducial</code> even when a common shift cancels. The claim envelope is now the extrema over start = <code>delta_common + eps_on</code>, stop = <code>delta_common + eps_off</code> with <code>|delta_common| &lt;= B_bundle</code> and <code>|eps_on|, |eps_off| &lt;= B_fiducial</code> independent. For nonnegative power the energy is monotone in each edge separately, so exact extrema are attained at the four edge corners with the common shift scanned continuously — the existing breakpoint-exact scan run per corner. The per-edge corner offset is <code>±(B_fiducial + wall_minus_monotonic_span)</code>: the span is a third disjoint per-edge error source, folded into the corners (delta-review amendment) rather than the frozen arms&#39; cruder <code>2·span·maxP</code> additive term, and the composed <code>anchor_bound_s</code> = <code>B_bundle + B_fiducial + span</code> governs the tail-sufficiency gate identically. Idle-subtracted and per-token envelopes additionally widen by <code>2·(B_fiducial + span)·P_idle</code> because independent edges vary the subtracted idle duration (delta re-audit catch). New registered method spelling for the 0.5.2/0.6.2 mints; v1/v2 spellings remain replay-read-only.</li> <li><strong>In-place revision of the unreleased mints.</strong> Reducer 0.5.2 / AXI 0.6.2 were never merged or used for stored artifacts; their envelope semantics are revised in place (no 0.5.3/0.6.3 inflation). Goldens regenerated and hand-verified against the formula.</li> <li><strong>Registry additions.</strong> The closed refusal vocabulary additionally includes <code>negative_power_sample</code> (negative rail power reaching the envelope/energy path breaks the monotonicity argument and refuses fail-closed) and <code>instrument_calibration_stale</code> (calibration artifacts now record capture wall time and a 24 h <code>max_age_s</code> validity horizon in protocol_v2; claim-time verification refuses missing/invalid capture time or age exceeded — a finite 40-pulse residual maximum is not an out-of-sample bound without recency enforcement). Instrument-evidence diagnostics additionally include <code>capture_time_missing_or_invalid</code> (a v2 capture without a valid recorded capture wall time is invalid at minting, with the reason stated rather than silent). All only refuse; the PENDING_DECISION_LOG_REGISTRATION exception is retired with this entry. Replay purity note: the 0.5.1/0.6.1 arms keep their frozen binding expectation against the protocol_v2.json bytes current at their mint (<code>REPLAY_PROTOCOL_V2_SHA256</code>); custody-manifest verification and the staleness horizon are current-mint gates only.</li> <li><strong>Environment admission consumes the full evidence object.</strong> The shared validator fails closed on <code>critical_environment_passed</code>, <code>reference_provenance_present</code>, per-run evaluation eligibility, guard observations, and schema identity — and the post-run environment observation passes through the failure predicate on claim/whole-window paths (a post-run critical-environment failure refuses claim eligibility). This closes the Window-A screensaver contamination class end-to-end.</li> <li><strong>Calibration custody verified at claim time.</strong> The reducer enforces the validation-manifest reference: in-bundle containment, manifest hash, and presence + sha256 of every manifest member; any failure refuses as <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>. Current-era (0.5.2/0.6.2) claim-bearing use requires a protocol_v2 calibration artifact.</li> <li><strong>Collection floors.</strong> The 1.0 s post-window dwell minimum is enforced on every collection path (controller default, schema minimum, campaign-policy validation); sub-minimum configs refuse at validation. Scope spelling (delta-review adjudication): controller/CLI pre-collection rejection applies wherever powermetrics telemetry collects; mock-backend runs are not dwell-gated at the controller (mock telemetry cannot reach any claim path), while the campaign-policy schema minimum applies universally. Inner phase/item/block/level window entries carry the whole-trace anchor/calibration/tail barrier stamps whenever the top-level barrier fires.</li> <li><strong>Cooldown terminal-evidence normativity documented.</strong> The required terminal JSONL row fields (<code>release</code>, <code>release_criteria_met_late</code>), the cap-first precedence rule (&quot;the cap is causal and wins&quot;), and rejection semantics are contract text in <code>docs/contracts/run_bundle_layout.md</code>, matching <code>joulewise/cooldown.py</code> exactly.</li> </ol> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-21 (third): provenance authentication rulings</h3> <p>Recorded by the lead after confirmation round 2 over <code>233e9e3</code> withheld sign-off (9 confirmed; the physics verified clean from every lens — all findings are provenance/governance). Rulings, implemented in the round-3 fix wave (frozen 0.5.1/0.6.1 replay semantics unchanged throughout):</p> <ol> <li><strong>Declared facts are authenticated against primary bytes.</strong> The calibration&#39;s declared <code>capture_wall_time_s</code> must agree (±1 s) with the capture time independently derived from the hash-verified source events — a stale calibration can no longer be relabeled fresh (the P0).</li> <li><strong>Freshness covers the whole measurement.</strong> The 24 h horizon binds both <code>run_started</code> and the measured window END: <code>capture &lt;= run_started</code> and <code>window_end &lt;= capture + max_age_s</code>, inclusive. Pre-run delays cannot carry sampling past the declared validity of its calibration.</li> <li><strong>Version identity is validated generically.</strong> Generic bundle validation checks <code>reducer_version</code> against the closed known set and the §8.1 version/event-semantics pairing rules as a validation-time structured problem (no wire-schema enum — frozen-arm byte replay preserved); an unsupported <code>--reducer-version</code> yields the standard structured refusal, never a traceback.</li> <li><strong>Stored verdicts are re-derived, never trusted.</strong> The whole-window verifier rejects duplicated NEG-8 core members (occurrence-count semantics) and re-derives the bracket verdict from member evidence; disagreement with the stored row is <code>whole_window_verdict_conflict</code>. Delta-review strengthening (lead ruling): the re-derivation tolerances come from the repo-REGISTERED campaign policy whose file hash matches the row&#39;s <code>policy_sha256</code> — the one trust anchor that does not terminate at bundle custody. Unknown policy hashes, and rows whose self-asserted tolerances disagree with the registered policy, refuse <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> before re-derivation. The custody boundary is otherwise explicit: a forger with bundle write access can rewrite row-internal hashes consistently, but cannot mint a matching tracked policy file.</li> <li><strong>Protocol identity is shape-authenticated.</strong> A v2 <code>protocol_id</code> requires the v2 estimator identity, capture/horizon fields, and v2 residual shape; v1-shaped bodies relabeled v2 refuse <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>.</li> <li><strong>Admission attempts have timing semantics.</strong> Attempt-ledger rows carry strictly increasing, non-overlapping declared windows on the strict path; violations refuse <code>environment_admission_missing</code>. 7a. <strong>(Fourth-wave addendum — claim-aggregation rulings, same date.)</strong> After confirmation round 3 over <code>0925480</code> (instrument core verified defensible on fresh head collections by every lens; all four P0s in the claim-aggregation layer), the lead ruled: (1) floors/MDEs widen by EXACT linear-corner evaluation over member envelope intervals — residual widening <code>w_i·(n−1)/n + Σ_{j≠i}w_j/n</code>, contrast widening <code>Σ|c_i|·w_i</code> — never a max-width shortcut, and the dominance refusal fires against the widened quantity; (2) admission is causally bound to its run: the final attempt window ends at-or-before window start within <code>MAX_ADMISSION_GAP_S = 600</code> (inclusive), the post-run observation is captured at-or-after window end, and attempt windows must contain their stage&#39;s recorded idle-capture interval; (3) the whole-window verifier re-derives CPU admission and adapter continuity from member-bundle primary evidence, refuses nonempty condition lists and undecodable log lines (laundering must require consistent cross-bundle forgery, never a one-line edit — full erasure resistance inside bundle custody is impossible and is recorded as the honest boundary); (4) NEG-8 reference energies are re-reduced from primary evidence at the current mint at claim time (minutes-scale cost accepted), with canonical-workload identity (<code>canonical_neg8_workload</code> + <code>scientific_config_sha256</code> against the custody-bound config) enforced; (5) the four byte-frozen goldens carry executable sha256 pins. Round-4 confirmation follow-ups (same date): the universal <code>clock_anchor_unresolved</code> barrier covers the <code>0.4.1</code>/<code>0.4.2</code> arms (every pre-repair wire, not only 0.5.0/0.6.0 — the former 0.4.x escape is closed and its test assertion inverted); the production trace-margin gate uses the full three-term composed bound including the wall-minus-monotonic span; campaign <code>ready_for_analysis</code> requires a registered claim-eligible mint (<code>0.5.2</code>/<code>0.6.2</code>; mock telemetry exempt — it can never bear claims). Recorded custody boundary: the 24 h calibration horizon compares host wall time, so an operator with host time control can evade it — accepted (host time integrity is an operator obligation, like bundle custody itself).</li> </ol> <p>7b. <strong>(Fifth-wave addendum — calibration epistemics, same date.)</strong> After confirmation round 5 over <code>09b5de6</code> (the P0 was statistical, not mechanical: a 40-pulse sample maximum is not an out-of-sample deterministic bound — 87.1% confidence on the 95th percentile vs the D-054 doctrine&#39;s n=59 for 95/95), the lead ruled: (1) <strong>protocol_v3</strong> raises the pulse count to 59, satisfying the repo&#39;s own nonparametric 95/95 doctrine; v3 is required for future claim-bearing calibration captures (v2 artifacts stay verifiable as this arc&#39;s validation evidence). (2) <strong>B_fiducial&#39;s epistemic status is stated honestly everywhere</strong>: a 95/95 nonparametric calibration bound, deterministic for claims only under REGISTERED transfer assumptions — T1 binding-vector stationarity, T2 the authenticated 24 h horizon, T3 load-regime transfer (calibration pulses are GPU-matmul under CPU-light load; sustained mixed-load transfer is an assumption; a loaded-calibration protocol variant is the registered roadmap mitigation). (3) <strong>Calibration bracketing is required for claim-bearing collections</strong>: two valid artifacts bracketing the window (pre at-or-before start, post at-or-after end, each within its own horizon), consumed as <code>max(pre, post)</code>, refusing <code>instrument_calibration_bracket_missing</code> or on bracket drift beyond <code>calibration_bracket_max_drift_s</code> (production 10 ms). Single-calibration reduction remains valid only for non-claim-bearing probe/exploratory use. (4) <strong>Environment state is window-enforced</strong>: per-interval thermal-pressure records are scanned over the measured window (<code>thermal_pressure_elevated_in_window</code> refusal); admission objects are recomputed from their embedded snapshots — a stored <code>eligible: true</code> is never trusted. (5) <strong>Loop-termination doctrine</strong>: convergence sign-off means zero UNADDRESSED P0/P1, where &quot;addressed&quot; includes a registered limitation with recorded justification, adjudicated by the lead. A physical instrument&#39;s uncertainty budget always rests on stated assumptions; the honest end state is registered assumptions, not infinite hardening. T3 is the first entry in that register. Round-6 follow-up (same date): the bracket maximum must be CONSUMED, not merely recorded — a claim refuses <code>calibration_bracket_exceeds_minted_bound</code> whenever <code>max(B_pre, B_post)</code> exceeds any member envelope&#39;s minted effective bound (the member must be re-reduced under the dominating calibration); the whole-window producer refuses duplicated member occurrences (occurrence-count doctrine at the producer, not just the claim verifier); the registered-policy trust anchor refuses duplicate-JSON-key policy bytes; and the standalone reducer horizon predicate upper-bounds <code>run_started</code> as well as the window end. Round-7 follow-ups (same date): the operative floor is the EXACT maximum of the complete D-054 guarded floor over the joint per-member interval corners (every component is convex in the member vector, so vertex enumeration is exact; n &lt;= 16 enumerated, larger widths refuse) — the linear-corner residual widening alone under-covered the Student-t prediction component; claim-licensing whole-window evidence requires the registered policy to be production-profile AND claim-bearing (exploratory rows can never license claims); the bracket-dominance gate authenticates each member&#39;s consumed bound from hash-verified calibration evidence (never the mint-time metadata scalar, whose disagreement is itself provenance-invalid); claim brackets accept protocol v3 artifacts ONLY (v2 stays valid as reduction/validation evidence). Round-8 follow-ups (2026-07-22): calibration identity is SEMANTICALLY authenticated, not just byte-authenticated — every calibration command event&#39;s two clocks (top-level <code>timestamp_s</code> and embedded ClockStamp epoch) must agree within 1 s on the strict path, and any event carrying a ClockStamp is skew-checked (the live artifact agrees within 0.205 ms; a shifted-freshness relabel now refuses); claim-time rederivation authenticates the EXECUTED v3 schedule (pulse durations, the deterministic van-der-Corput gap sequence within ±0.25 s, ≥4.5 s commanded-quiet baselines) so phase-locked or degenerate captures cannot claim the 95/95 identity; and the canonical floor/MDE artifact carries the corner-widened floor additively (validator recomputes it; the analysis engine consumes the WIDENED guarded floor as operative) — closing the honest-artifact-fails-closed gap so a sound end-to-end floor/MDE handoff exists. Registry additions for this wave: <code>instrument_calibration_bracket_missing</code>, <code>calibration_bracket_exceeds_minted_bound</code>, (claim-bearing window not bracketed by two authenticated, fresh calibration artifacts, or bracket drift beyond the registered tolerance) and <code>thermal_pressure_elevated_in_window</code> (per-interval thermal-pressure records non-nominal — or missing on the strict path — anywhere in the admission-to-window span). Both only refuse; the PENDING_DECISION_LOG_REGISTRATION exception for them is retired with this entry.</p> <ol start="7"> <li><p><strong>Sign-off evidence must be head-minted.</strong> Any artifact or re-reduction quoted as validation evidence for a head must be regenerated AT that head (the pre-233e9e3 rederived calibration artifact lacks the horizon fields the head requires, and the probe re-reductions predate the strict calibration gates — both are re-minted at the final head before the sign-off record is written). Claim-bearing measurement additionally requires fresh live [QUIET-MAC] calibration under protocol v3 (59 pulses, fifth-wave addendum), bracketing the window, within 24 h of collection.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Confirmation round 9 (2026-07-22, FINAL under the Ed-ratified cap) — outcome and registered limitation L1.</strong> The round-9 review over head 040ca3a confirmed the fiducial chain, reduce-side verification taxonomy, and contract coherence clean, with ONE surviving blocker (CR9-1, repro-backed, lead-reproduced): the canonical floor/MDE artifact is SELF-ATTESTING about its admissible half-widths and campaign membership — <code>validate_floor_artifact</code> recomputes widened floors only from artifact-internal widths, and evidence binding authenticates identities, hashes, and ordering but neither rederives source widths nor requires complete governed campaign membership. A substituted artifact with understated widths (or one omitting a member) validates, binds, and licenses an exact claim floor. Per the loop-termination doctrine (clause 5), the lead adjudicates this a REGISTERED LIMITATION rather than a tenth round:</p> <ul> <li><strong>L1 (registered): canonical floor artifacts are not independently claim-licensing.</strong> Until floor↔extraction binding lands, a claim-bearing analysis may consume a floor artifact ONLY when it was produced by the governed extraction in the same custody session as the analysis (same run manifest; extraction gates demonstrably executed). Standalone or externally supplied floor artifacts are non-claim-bearing evidence. Justification: the exposure is artifact substitution or a defective producer BETWEEN extraction and analysis; an honest same-session pipeline computes widths and membership under the already -hardened extraction gates, so no measurement this program will make under L1&#39;s workflow rule is affected. The gap is a third-party verifiability deficit, not an instrument-physics defect.</li> <li><strong>Queued fix (next cycle, P1):</strong> bind each canonical floor cell to its extraction report and source-member disposition (or rederive the extraction gates and widths at binding), refusing on any stored width/corner mismatch or membership deviation, with integration regressions for width substitution and member omission (TASK_QUEUE FLOOR-BIND-01). Round-9 verification note: the focused 357-test review surface passed at the head in-session; the lead&#39;s full-suite gate over the identical tree content (2088 passed / 15 skipped / 1570 subtests / 0 failures) stands as the aggregate confirmation.</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><strong>Live collection arc (2026-07-22/23) — collection-path regressions, occurrence supersession, and basis-scoped verdicts.</strong> The first live Window-A members after sign-off exposed collection-path defects invisible to nine review rounds without hardware; each was fixed under the ratified contracts (PR #80 canonical-attempt promotion + sole-sampler gapless design; PR #81 idle-slice cursor after forensics proved the slicer&#39;s own parsing contaminated the admission interval at the real ~120 ms powermetrics cadence). Two doctrine amendments were then ruled by the lead when the whole-window verdict path contradicted operational guidance (both defaults preserved, both overrides explicit and auditable):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Occurrence supersession (amends the round-6 occurrence-count doctrine):</strong> duplicated member occurrences still REFUSE by default; a duplicate may resolve to the present bundle only when an explicit operator supersession artifact (append-only, hash-sealed, naming the superseded occurrence, quarantine destination, and reason — <code>--record-supersession</code>) exists; two present bundles always refuse.</li> <li><strong>Basis-scoped whole-window verdicts:</strong> latest-wins remains rejected (verdict-shopping prevention); every verdict records a canonical evaluation-basis hash (member occurrence set + calibration bracket set<ul> <li>policy) and binds only that basis; consumers match the claim&#39;s basis; legacy basis-less verdict rows never govern new claims. Diagnostic-cascade decoupling and whole-window waiver consumption landed in the same wave. Windows a5 (108 members) and prior attempts remain NON-claim-bearing as whole windows (true clock-anchor refusal on one member; NEG-8 end reference measured ~2 h post-collection failed the drift gate at 0.778 J — the instrument correctly refusing a stale bracket); their corpora stand as instrument-proving evidence. The next clean bracketed window is the first claim attempt.</li> </ul> </li> </ul> </li> <li><p><strong>NEG-8 drift-gate estimand ruling (2026-07-24; lead-ruled; RATIFIED in amended SCREEN+BUDGET form by the clause-10 addendum below — this original gross-only form was superseded the same day and never collected under).</strong> The whole-window drift adjudication proved the gate as previously implemented compared the two reference cells&#39; admissible envelopes at opposite corners (~0.9-1.5 J stacked) against an underived 0.05 J constant — structurally unpassable even for a physically perfect window (a8 measured point drift 0.006718 J over 2.96 h on ~38.5 J references). Ruling: the gate estimand is POINT DRIFT abs(end_point_gross − start_point_gross); the idle-subtracted point drift and the opposite-corner envelope statistic are recorded diagnostics, never gating (envelope stacking double-counts instrument uncertainty already composed into floor envelopes). The bound is DERIVED: a hash-sealed <code>joulewise.neg8_drift_bound.v1</code> artifact minted by governed CLI from a named settled-reference corpus (n&gt;=10, predeclared estimator <code>d054_point_contrast_guard_v1</code> = max(sample_range_j, t_{0.975,n-1}·s·sqrt(2))), consumed with full provenance in the verdict output. Registry addition: <code>neg8_drift_bound_underived</code> (fail-closed refusal whenever no valid governed bound artifact exists). Windows a6/a8 may be re-verdicted under the derived bound (with explicit waivers for aborted-member fragments); a5 and a7 remain refused on their genuine grounds.</p> </li> </ol> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum — debate and Ed ratification (2026-07-24).</strong> Per Ed&#39;s direction the ruling was formally debated with the peer model before ratification. The peer DISAGREED with the ruling as written on one structural point and was adjudicated correct: the point-drift statistic is the right estimand but an anomaly screen is not proof of stability — passing the gate must never erase observed drift from the claim error budget (consistent with the repo&#39;s own D-054/D-057 language). Ed RATIFIED the amended SCREEN + BUDGET design (the debate&#39;s option F, full variant, Ed explicitly directing the maximal build): per-claim-family point-drift screens (gross AND idle-subtracted, each with its own derived bound); per-family drift ALLOWANCES propagated additively into every floor/claim envelope of the window, never zero even on passing windows (allowance = max(observed excursion, derived repeatability bound)); replicated endpoint references (n=3 per endpoint, means with standard errors) and one midpoint reference prospectively, with the allowance taken over the maximum absolute excursion across sampled points; drift-bound artifacts carry a freshness horizon and re-derivation triggers (OS/build, power-supply, calibration-identity changes) with a distinct stale-bound refusal spelling; legacy pair-only windows evaluate under the single-member-endpoint minimum. Ed&#39;s recorded guardrails: watch the RIGOR SPIRAL (floors inflating past the effect sizes the science needs — monitor floor-vs-expected-effect at every extraction) and NO INVENTED PHYSICS (no functional form without a defensible basis; stated limitations beat unjustified formulas). Guiding light for all measurement-program decisions: the Splitwise replication (P2-006); methodology grounding against the Splitwise paper and comparable energy-measurement literature is in flight and feeds the collection design. Economics note recorded: Ed values artifact quality over time/tokens/machine-hours (project runs months ahead of deadline).</p> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum 2 — screen+budget wave registry + anchor-fallback gate ruling (lead, 2026-07-24).</strong> Registers the wave&#39;s spellings in the D-078 closed registry: <code>neg8_idle_sub_drift_bound_underived</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_idle_sub_abs_delta_exceeded</code>, and <code>neg8_drift_bound_stale</code> (freshness horizon exceeded or re-derivation trigger fired) — the ratified clause-10 design&#39;s concrete spellings — plus <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code> (unwaivable, no waiver spelling exists: a fallback-clock-anchored member may not anchor a floor or claim cell; in a floor cell it is an unwaivable re-run trigger). The latter is a LEAD-INITIATED ruling from the 2026-07-24 a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (<code>a7_vs_a5_prefill_scatter_analysis.md</code>): a7&#39;s 11.85 J prefill &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member (r03), half-width-zero envelope — instrument artifact (true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J). Flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review. Also registered (fix-round F3): <code>whole_window_drift_allowance_unrecorded</code> (passing basis-bearing verdict with no authenticated per-family allowance, or a claim missing its named allowance term — refuse, never zero; in both the floor-extraction and reducer vocabularies, mirroring <code>interpolation_bound_unrecorded</code>).</p> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum 3 — terminal mock bar (lead, 2026-07-24).</strong> The ratified premise &quot;mock telemetry can never bear claims&quot; had no terminal enforcement at the analysis claim boundary: honest mock members reached floor cells and claim evidence with the mock-exempted barriers disabled. Registered spelling: <code>mock_telemetry_claim_ineligible</code> (claim-bearing consumption of a member whose custody-bound config telemetry backend is the mock class; refuse — development-only evidence, no waiver spelling exists). Mockness derives from the custody-bound config (<code>hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bytes bound via <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>), never from summary/metadata labels alone; where such a config exists, config/metadata/summary telemetry identities must agree by backend class (governed <code>mock:*</code> tags are mock class) or the bundle is strict-invalid. Config absence is non-production evidence (fixture-only permissive paths keep their ratified intent). Lead-initiated; flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review.</p> <ol start="11"> <li><strong>Attribution-limited detection floors — Ed-RATIFIED amendment (2026-07-25).</strong> The first collection under the merged SCREEN+BUDGET rules (windows a9, a10; both whole-window verdicts PASSED) could not produce a floor: all three of a10&#39;s phase-absolute cells refuse <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code>. <strong>Finding: the instrument is ATTRIBUTION-limited, not NOISE-limited.</strong> Repeatability is 0.29-0.49 J on ~50 J points (and a settled reference pair three hours apart agreed to 0.007 J), but each member carries a clock-anchor-shift envelope of ~0.7-1.0 J: a +/-31 ms window shift across a phase boundary where power swings ~33 W mis-attributes ~1 J between prefill and decode. The composed bound is additive and measured — fiducial 24.9 ms (80-87%) plus bundle-local 3.3-6.1 ms plus edge span. Because repeatability will always beat attribution here, the refusal is STRUCTURALLY PERMANENT: no future phase corpus can pass it and there is nothing to re-collect around.</li> </ol> <p> <strong>Alternatives measured and eliminated</strong> (authenticated replay, 2026-07-25): (a) the calibration-bracket gap is NOT the cause — every cell refuses under both its minted and its post-bracket bound (delta +0.167 ms); (b) instrument tightening cannot rescue it — extraction would require a 10x (decode) to 32x (prefill) bound reduction, and each cell&#39;s bundle-local term ALONE (3.3-6.1 ms) already exceeds the entire required bound (0.99-2.9 ms), so even a perfect fiducial calibration would still refuse; (c) coarser granularity does not rescue it — request-level cells replayed on a10 and a8 have smaller envelopes (1.5-1.9 J) but still dominate and still refuse; (d) an ABBA common-mode estimator gives a real 3x gain (a5 decode 6.46 J -&gt; 2.13 J) but remains above that cell&#39;s 0.60 J point floor. The labelled path below is therefore not the preferred option among several — it is the only remaining path to any detection floor at all, at any granularity, on this instrument.</p> <p> <strong>Ruling (Ed-ratified).</strong> D-054 registers the detection floor as a practical prediction bound on FALSE OBSERVED EFFECTS, not as a repeatability statistic; a false observed effect may arise from scatter OR from anchor mis-attribution, and the corner-widened maximum is exactly the largest false effect this instrument can produce. <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code> therefore becomes a LABELLED CLAIM PATH rather than a hard refusal: extraction publishes the widened floor with a <code>floor_source</code> field naming the dominant term (here <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>) and retains the point floor separately as the repeatability diagnostic. The gate keeps its real function — preventing a repeatability-only number from publishing as if it were the whole story — while no longer conflating &quot;unsound corpus&quot; with &quot;instrument-limited floor&quot;. a10 is sound.</p> <p> <strong>Binding condition — SINGLE-COUNT DISCIPLINE (Ed: &quot;the cost seems sensible as long as it&#39;s noted&quot;).</strong> The floor gate now contains the anchor term, and each claim&#39;s decision interval separately consumes the member&#39;s <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>. These are different objects (calibration false-effect bound vs claim-side measurement uncertainty) and both are legitimate, but the consequence is that the effective clearable effect is FLOOR + CLAIM-SIDE BOUND (~5 J for phase contrasts), not the floor alone. Every artifact publishing an attribution-limited floor must state this explicitly so that neither term is later removed as an apparent double count. Science must be sized to the ~5 J bar; Splitwise-class effects (tens of percent of tens of joules) clear it with margin.</p> <p> <strong>Not authorised by this amendment:</strong> any instrument-tightening program. Revisit only if a pilot shows target effects below ~3x the widened floor. The free lever is workload sizing — attribution error is approximately duration-independent while effects scale with workload, so longer prefill/decode raises effect-to-floor linearly at zero instrument cost (queue FLOOR-WORKLOAD-SIZING-01).</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <strong aria-current="page">Recent</strong> · <a href="decision_log_archive_1.html">Archive 1</a></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

<p>The guide and complete decision index continue on Archive 1; the navigation on this page links every rendered part.</p> <span id="d-078"></span><h2 id="d-078-soundness-gate-no-claim-bearing-extraction-from-time-anchor-defective-powermetrics-corpora">D-078: Soundness gate — no claim-bearing extraction from time-anchor-defective powermetrics corpora</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-19. Owner: lead session under Ed&#39;s soundness-audit directive; recorded so the gate binds future sessions immediately. Status update 2026-07-22: the gate has been operative under Ed&#39;s direction through the entire repair arc, and Ed explicitly ratified the close-out cap (clause 8); formal ratification of this original text rides the PR #79 review (Ed may amend).</p> <p>The 2026-07-19 measurement-soundness audit (<code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>; all P0 findings lead-verified from primary evidence) found that powermetrics trace timestamps are misaligned with runtime events at the ~0.5–1 s scale (pre-spawn/first-parse midpoint anchor), making request/phase/item point energies physically non-attributable as recorded across ALL existing powermetrics corpora, including the 2026-07-17 published floor extraction.</p> <p>Binding until amended:</p> <ol> <li>No claim-bearing floor, MDE, or L2/L3 energy claim may be published from any corpus collected under the defective anchor. Existing corpora are instrument/calibration evidence only.</li> <li>Extraction must treat <code>window_evidence_precheck</code> as a hard gate and must join campaign-log cooldown/admission evidence (cap hits are not clean n). &quot;Claim-eligible&quot; narrative language may describe METRIC-level eligibility only, never source provenance alone.</li> <li>The repair path (roadmap Phase 0, <code>docs/phase_2/splitwise_replication_roadmap.md</code>): tight causal anchor + anchor-shift joule envelope in reduction, analysis-engine 0.5.0/v2 wire compat, CPU-aware idle admission, prospective NEG-8 acceptance threshold. Stored summaries are never rewritten; fixes are prospective.</li> <li>The 2026-07-17 published floor table is caveated in PROJECT_STATUS pending re-extraction; advisor-brief/site correction timing is Ed&#39;s deployment decision (D-068).</li> </ol> <p>Revisit trigger: Phase 0 repair lands with live pulse-validation evidence, or Ed rules a different salvage/disposition for existing corpora.</p> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-20: fail-closed vocabulary and immutable summaries</h3> <p>Additive amendment under the adversarial soundness fix round. The following spellings are the binding, closed registry for D-078 claim refusals and campaign conditions. Consumers preserve these strings verbatim; an unknown claim/refusal spelling never becomes a pass.</p> <ul> <li>Reducer/analysis claim barriers: <code>nonpositive_window_duration</code>, <code>insufficient_in_window_samples</code>, <code>cadence_ratio_unrecorded</code>, <code>cadence_ratio_below_threshold</code>, <code>clock_bound_unrecorded</code>, <code>clock_bound_exceeds_quarter_window</code>, <code>interpolation_bound_unrecorded</code>, <code>drift_term_unknown</code>, <code>idle_baseline_unrecorded</code>, <code>cooldown_cap_hit</code>, <code>environment_admission_failed</code>, <code>environment_override</code>, <code>environment_admission_missing</code>, <code>cpu_admission_unenforced</code>, <code>clock_anchor_unresolved</code>, <code>anchor_energy_envelope_unrecorded</code>, <code>anchor_energy_envelope_exceeds_quarter_metric</code>, <code>instrument_calibration_missing</code>, <code>instrument_calibration_mismatch</code>, and <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>.</li> <li>Floor-extraction refusals: <code>bundle_missing</code>, <code>summary_unreadable</code>, <code>bundle_strict_invalid</code>, <code>bundle_hash_unresolved</code>, <code>bundle_status_not_succeeded</code>, <code>reducer_wire_unknown</code>, <code>idle_method_pair_invalid</code>, <code>metric_missing_or_nonfinite</code>, <code>window_evidence_precheck_failed</code>, <code>campaign_cooldown_evidence_missing</code>, <code>cooldown_cap_hit_unverified</code>, <code>campaign_member_omitted_from_spec</code>, <code>campaign_member_unattributable</code>, <code>cap_hit_drift_term_unavailable</code>, <code>insufficient_members_after_exclusion</code>, plus every applicable reducer barrier above and <code>whole_window_neg8_verdict_missing</code>, <code>whole_window_neg8_verdict_failed</code>, <code>adapter_continuity_evidence_missing</code>, <code>adapter_continuity_failed</code>, <code>cpu_admission_core_missing</code>, and <code>cpu_admission_core_failed</code>.</li> <li>Idle-admission/campaign conditions: <code>cpu_baseline_telemetry_missing</code>, <code>cpu_baseline_telemetry_malformed</code>, <code>cpu_baseline_sample_count_insufficient</code>, <code>cpu_busy_ratio_p95_exceeded</code>, <code>processor_combined_power_w_p95_exceeded</code>, <code>gpu_idle_admission_not_passed</code>, <code>gpu_idle_admission_unknown</code>, <code>adapter_observations_missing</code>, <code>adapter_wattage_unknown</code>, <code>adapter_wattage_discontinuity</code>, <code>adapter_description_changed</code>, <code>adapter_power_source_changed</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_missing</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_reference_invalid</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_abs_delta_exceeded</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_rel_delta_exceeded</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_not_evaluated</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_ambiguous_reference</code>, <code>idle_admission_attempt_ledger_invalid</code>, <code>idle_admission_extension_unconfigured</code>, <code>whole_window_bundle_invalid</code>, <code>whole_window_campaign_membership_unresolved</code>, and <code>whole_window_campaign_membership_ambiguous</code>.</li> <li>Instrument-evidence diagnostics: <code>pulse_detection_incomplete</code>, <code>spurious_plateau_detected</code>, <code>residual_interval_unbounded</code>, <code>not_all_pulses_detected</code>, <code>binding_fields_missing:</code>, <code>pulse_count_below_protocol:</code>, and <code>raw_or_event_hash_missing_or_invalid</code>. These diagnostics can only make <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>; they never directly license a claim.</li> </ul> <p>Governance ruling GOV-02: D-078 supersedes only D-028&#39;s former exception that allowed <code>summary_metrics.json</code> to be rewritten after finalization. Stored summary bytes are now immutable evidence. Post-hoc reduction writes a new, non-clobbering artifact (including the repaired anchor envelope) or refuses; the raw-artifact immutability and pure-reducer portions of D-002/D-028 remain in force. Frozen 0.5.0/0.6.0 numeric semantics remain replayable and are not claim-bearing merely because they can be read.</p> <h3>D-078 additive registry addendum — 2026-07-20: causal-set repair</h3> <p>The closed registry additionally includes floor/whole-window barriers <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code>, <code>whole_window_verdict_coverage_incomplete</code>, <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code>, and <code>whole_window_verdict_conflict</code>. Instrument-evidence diagnostics additionally include <code>no_plateau_interior_intervals</code>, <code>plateau_below_minimum</code>, <code>robust_snr_below_minimum</code>, <code>edge_coverage_missing</code>, <code>model_fit_not_significant</code>, and <code>fitted_shift_exceeds_validation_limit</code>. These additions only refuse or widen uncertainty; none can license a claim.</p> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-21: convergence fix wave (lead adjudications)</h3> <p>Recorded by the lead after the two-round cross-model convergence loop over <code>impl/p0-instrument-repair</code> (round-2 and round-3 fix waves; council log carries the layer accounting). Six rulings:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Additive causal-bound composition.</strong> <code>B_effective = B_bundle + B_fiducial</code> replaces <code>max(B_bundle, B_fiducial)</code>. The bundle-local censored-constraint anchor interval and the instrument&#39;s emission-lag bound sit on disjoint causal links; no containment proof exists, so <code>max()</code> under-composes. <code>B_fiducial</code> itself additively folds in the calibration capture&#39;s own trace-anchor bound. The prior <code>max()</code> text in this log is superseded prospectively; stored summaries are never rewritten.</li> <li><strong>Identity bump, not in-place semantics change.</strong> The additive composition, fiducial protocol_v2 physics (<code>joint_loss_sublevel_interval_branch_v2</code> full 2-D branch-and-bound region), and the stricter evidence-admission semantics are minted as reducer <code>0.5.2</code> / AXI <code>0.6.2</code> with <code>configs/calibration/powermetrics_fiducial/protocol_v2.json</code>. <code>0.5.1</code> / <code>0.6.1</code> and <code>protocol_v1.json</code> remain byte-frozen replay arms.</li> <li><strong>Superseded arms are claim-ineligible.</strong> <code>0.5.1</code>/<code>0.6.1</code> summaries refuse claim-bearing use with a registered refusal (superseded max-composition envelope semantics); <code>0.5.2</code>/<code>0.6.2</code> are the sole claim-eligible mints.</li> <li><strong>Registry additions (closing the F11/PENDING exception).</strong> The closed refusal vocabulary additionally includes <code>token_count_stream_chunk_fallback</code> (renamed from the source-label reuse of <code>stream_chunk_fallback</code>), <code>pulse_calibration_rollover_gate_timeout</code> (pre-workload rollover gate timeout now refuses fail-closed, no artifact minting), and <code>post_window_trace_tail_shorter_than_anchor_bound</code> (reduce-time refusal when the post-window trace tail cannot support the composed anchor bound; collection policy raises the minimum post-window dwell to 1.0 s). These only refuse; none can license a claim.</li> <li><strong>Registry closure is one-way by design.</strong> Every emitted spelling must be registered here; a registered spelling with no current emission site (e.g. <code>window_evidence_precheck_failed</code>, <code>cap_hit_drift_term_unavailable</code>) is permitted — unemittable names cannot launder anything.</li> <li><strong>Member-level <code>claim_evidence_flags</code> is an all-leaf union — documented, not changed.</strong> Adjudicated a documentation defect only: the union is fail-safe (it can only over-flag, never over-admit) and gating decisions read the per-metric leaves. Scope documented in <code>docs/contracts/run_bundle_layout.md</code>; no wire rename.</li> </ol> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-21 (second): two-edge envelope and confirmation-round rulings</h3> <p>Recorded by the lead after the first confirmation round over <code>5093355</code> correctly withheld sign-off (fresh Sol xhigh audit; 8 confirmed findings, one P0). Rulings:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Corner-composed two-edge envelope (P0 repair).</strong> The calibration fits independent start-edge and stop-edge emission lags; a single common trace shift under-covers because independent endpoint errors move energy by up to <code>2·P·B_fiducial</code> even when a common shift cancels. The claim envelope is now the extrema over start = <code>delta_common + eps_on</code>, stop = <code>delta_common + eps_off</code> with <code>|delta_common| &lt;= B_bundle</code> and <code>|eps_on|, |eps_off| &lt;= B_fiducial</code> independent. For nonnegative power the energy is monotone in each edge separately, so exact extrema are attained at the four edge corners with the common shift scanned continuously — the existing breakpoint-exact scan run per corner. The per-edge corner offset is <code>±(B_fiducial + wall_minus_monotonic_span)</code>: the span is a third disjoint per-edge error source, folded into the corners (delta-review amendment) rather than the frozen arms&#39; cruder <code>2·span·maxP</code> additive term, and the composed <code>anchor_bound_s</code> = <code>B_bundle + B_fiducial + span</code> governs the tail-sufficiency gate identically. Idle-subtracted and per-token envelopes additionally widen by <code>2·(B_fiducial + span)·P_idle</code> because independent edges vary the subtracted idle duration (delta re-audit catch). New registered method spelling for the 0.5.2/0.6.2 mints; v1/v2 spellings remain replay-read-only.</li> <li><strong>In-place revision of the unreleased mints.</strong> Reducer 0.5.2 / AXI 0.6.2 were never merged or used for stored artifacts; their envelope semantics are revised in place (no 0.5.3/0.6.3 inflation). Goldens regenerated and hand-verified against the formula.</li> <li><strong>Registry additions.</strong> The closed refusal vocabulary additionally includes <code>negative_power_sample</code> (negative rail power reaching the envelope/energy path breaks the monotonicity argument and refuses fail-closed) and <code>instrument_calibration_stale</code> (calibration artifacts now record capture wall time and a 24 h <code>max_age_s</code> validity horizon in protocol_v2; claim-time verification refuses missing/invalid capture time or age exceeded — a finite 40-pulse residual maximum is not an out-of-sample bound without recency enforcement). Instrument-evidence diagnostics additionally include <code>capture_time_missing_or_invalid</code> (a v2 capture without a valid recorded capture wall time is invalid at minting, with the reason stated rather than silent). All only refuse; the PENDING_DECISION_LOG_REGISTRATION exception is retired with this entry. Replay purity note: the 0.5.1/0.6.1 arms keep their frozen binding expectation against the protocol_v2.json bytes current at their mint (<code>REPLAY_PROTOCOL_V2_SHA256</code>); custody-manifest verification and the staleness horizon are current-mint gates only.</li> <li><strong>Environment admission consumes the full evidence object.</strong> The shared validator fails closed on <code>critical_environment_passed</code>, <code>reference_provenance_present</code>, per-run evaluation eligibility, guard observations, and schema identity — and the post-run environment observation passes through the failure predicate on claim/whole-window paths (a post-run critical-environment failure refuses claim eligibility). This closes the Window-A screensaver contamination class end-to-end.</li> <li><strong>Calibration custody verified at claim time.</strong> The reducer enforces the validation-manifest reference: in-bundle containment, manifest hash, and presence + sha256 of every manifest member; any failure refuses as <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>. Current-era (0.5.2/0.6.2) claim-bearing use requires a protocol_v2 calibration artifact.</li> <li><strong>Collection floors.</strong> The 1.0 s post-window dwell minimum is enforced on every collection path (controller default, schema minimum, campaign-policy validation); sub-minimum configs refuse at validation. Scope spelling (delta-review adjudication): controller/CLI pre-collection rejection applies wherever powermetrics telemetry collects; mock-backend runs are not dwell-gated at the controller (mock telemetry cannot reach any claim path), while the campaign-policy schema minimum applies universally. Inner phase/item/block/level window entries carry the whole-trace anchor/calibration/tail barrier stamps whenever the top-level barrier fires.</li> <li><strong>Cooldown terminal-evidence normativity documented.</strong> The required terminal JSONL row fields (<code>release</code>, <code>release_criteria_met_late</code>), the cap-first precedence rule (&quot;the cap is causal and wins&quot;), and rejection semantics are contract text in <code>docs/contracts/run_bundle_layout.md</code>, matching <code>joulewise/cooldown.py</code> exactly.</li> </ol> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-21 (third): provenance authentication rulings</h3> <p>Recorded by the lead after confirmation round 2 over <code>233e9e3</code> withheld sign-off (9 confirmed; the physics verified clean from every lens — all findings are provenance/governance). Rulings, implemented in the round-3 fix wave (frozen 0.5.1/0.6.1 replay semantics unchanged throughout):</p> <ol> <li><strong>Declared facts are authenticated against primary bytes.</strong> The calibration&#39;s declared <code>capture_wall_time_s</code> must agree (±1 s) with the capture time independently derived from the hash-verified source events — a stale calibration can no longer be relabeled fresh (the P0).</li> <li><strong>Freshness covers the whole measurement.</strong> The 24 h horizon binds both <code>run_started</code> and the measured window END: <code>capture &lt;= run_started</code> and <code>window_end &lt;= capture + max_age_s</code>, inclusive. Pre-run delays cannot carry sampling past the declared validity of its calibration.</li> <li><strong>Version identity is validated generically.</strong> Generic bundle validation checks <code>reducer_version</code> against the closed known set and the §8.1 version/event-semantics pairing rules as a validation-time structured problem (no wire-schema enum — frozen-arm byte replay preserved); an unsupported <code>--reducer-version</code> yields the standard structured refusal, never a traceback.</li> <li><strong>Stored verdicts are re-derived, never trusted.</strong> The whole-window verifier rejects duplicated NEG-8 core members (occurrence-count semantics) and re-derives the bracket verdict from member evidence; disagreement with the stored row is <code>whole_window_verdict_conflict</code>. Delta-review strengthening (lead ruling): the re-derivation tolerances come from the repo-REGISTERED campaign policy whose file hash matches the row&#39;s <code>policy_sha256</code> — the one trust anchor that does not terminate at bundle custody. Unknown policy hashes, and rows whose self-asserted tolerances disagree with the registered policy, refuse <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> before re-derivation. The custody boundary is otherwise explicit: a forger with bundle write access can rewrite row-internal hashes consistently, but cannot mint a matching tracked policy file.</li> <li><strong>Protocol identity is shape-authenticated.</strong> A v2 <code>protocol_id</code> requires the v2 estimator identity, capture/horizon fields, and v2 residual shape; v1-shaped bodies relabeled v2 refuse <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>.</li> <li><strong>Admission attempts have timing semantics.</strong> Attempt-ledger rows carry strictly increasing, non-overlapping declared windows on the strict path; violations refuse <code>environment_admission_missing</code>. 7a. <strong>(Fourth-wave addendum — claim-aggregation rulings, same date.)</strong> After confirmation round 3 over <code>0925480</code> (instrument core verified defensible on fresh head collections by every lens; all four P0s in the claim-aggregation layer), the lead ruled: (1) floors/MDEs widen by EXACT linear-corner evaluation over member envelope intervals — residual widening <code>w_i·(n−1)/n + Σ_{j≠i}w_j/n</code>, contrast widening <code>Σ|c_i|·w_i</code> — never a max-width shortcut, and the dominance refusal fires against the widened quantity; (2) admission is causally bound to its run: the final attempt window ends at-or-before window start within <code>MAX_ADMISSION_GAP_S = 600</code> (inclusive), the post-run observation is captured at-or-after window end, and attempt windows must contain their stage&#39;s recorded idle-capture interval; (3) the whole-window verifier re-derives CPU admission and adapter continuity from member-bundle primary evidence, refuses nonempty condition lists and undecodable log lines (laundering must require consistent cross-bundle forgery, never a one-line edit — full erasure resistance inside bundle custody is impossible and is recorded as the honest boundary); (4) NEG-8 reference energies are re-reduced from primary evidence at the current mint at claim time (minutes-scale cost accepted), with canonical-workload identity (<code>canonical_neg8_workload</code> + <code>scientific_config_sha256</code> against the custody-bound config) enforced; (5) the four byte-frozen goldens carry executable sha256 pins. Round-4 confirmation follow-ups (same date): the universal <code>clock_anchor_unresolved</code> barrier covers the <code>0.4.1</code>/<code>0.4.2</code> arms (every pre-repair wire, not only 0.5.0/0.6.0 — the former 0.4.x escape is closed and its test assertion inverted); the production trace-margin gate uses the full three-term composed bound including the wall-minus-monotonic span; campaign <code>ready_for_analysis</code> requires a registered claim-eligible mint (<code>0.5.2</code>/<code>0.6.2</code>; mock telemetry exempt — it can never bear claims). Recorded custody boundary: the 24 h calibration horizon compares host wall time, so an operator with host time control can evade it — accepted (host time integrity is an operator obligation, like bundle custody itself).</li> </ol> <p>7b. <strong>(Fifth-wave addendum — calibration epistemics, same date.)</strong> After confirmation round 5 over <code>09b5de6</code> (the P0 was statistical, not mechanical: a 40-pulse sample maximum is not an out-of-sample deterministic bound — 87.1% confidence on the 95th percentile vs the D-054 doctrine&#39;s n=59 for 95/95), the lead ruled: (1) <strong>protocol_v3</strong> raises the pulse count to 59, satisfying the repo&#39;s own nonparametric 95/95 doctrine; v3 is required for future claim-bearing calibration captures (v2 artifacts stay verifiable as this arc&#39;s validation evidence). (2) <strong>B_fiducial&#39;s epistemic status is stated honestly everywhere</strong>: a 95/95 nonparametric calibration bound, deterministic for claims only under REGISTERED transfer assumptions — T1 binding-vector stationarity, T2 the authenticated 24 h horizon, T3 load-regime transfer (calibration pulses are GPU-matmul under CPU-light load; sustained mixed-load transfer is an assumption; a loaded-calibration protocol variant is the registered roadmap mitigation). (3) <strong>Calibration bracketing is required for claim-bearing collections</strong>: two valid artifacts bracketing the window (pre at-or-before start, post at-or-after end, each within its own horizon), consumed as <code>max(pre, post)</code>, refusing <code>instrument_calibration_bracket_missing</code> or on bracket drift beyond <code>calibration_bracket_max_drift_s</code> (production 10 ms). Single-calibration reduction remains valid only for non-claim-bearing probe/exploratory use. (4) <strong>Environment state is window-enforced</strong>: per-interval thermal-pressure records are scanned over the measured window (<code>thermal_pressure_elevated_in_window</code> refusal); admission objects are recomputed from their embedded snapshots — a stored <code>eligible: true</code> is never trusted. (5) <strong>Loop-termination doctrine</strong>: convergence sign-off means zero UNADDRESSED P0/P1, where &quot;addressed&quot; includes a registered limitation with recorded justification, adjudicated by the lead. A physical instrument&#39;s uncertainty budget always rests on stated assumptions; the honest end state is registered assumptions, not infinite hardening. T3 is the first entry in that register. Round-6 follow-up (same date): the bracket maximum must be CONSUMED, not merely recorded — a claim refuses <code>calibration_bracket_exceeds_minted_bound</code> whenever <code>max(B_pre, B_post)</code> exceeds any member envelope&#39;s minted effective bound (the member must be re-reduced under the dominating calibration); the whole-window producer refuses duplicated member occurrences (occurrence-count doctrine at the producer, not just the claim verifier); the registered-policy trust anchor refuses duplicate-JSON-key policy bytes; and the standalone reducer horizon predicate upper-bounds <code>run_started</code> as well as the window end. Round-7 follow-ups (same date): the operative floor is the EXACT maximum of the complete D-054 guarded floor over the joint per-member interval corners (every component is convex in the member vector, so vertex enumeration is exact; n &lt;= 16 enumerated, larger widths refuse) — the linear-corner residual widening alone under-covered the Student-t prediction component; claim-licensing whole-window evidence requires the registered policy to be production-profile AND claim-bearing (exploratory rows can never license claims); the bracket-dominance gate authenticates each member&#39;s consumed bound from hash-verified calibration evidence (never the mint-time metadata scalar, whose disagreement is itself provenance-invalid); claim brackets accept protocol v3 artifacts ONLY (v2 stays valid as reduction/validation evidence). Round-8 follow-ups (2026-07-22): calibration identity is SEMANTICALLY authenticated, not just byte-authenticated — every calibration command event&#39;s two clocks (top-level <code>timestamp_s</code> and embedded ClockStamp epoch) must agree within 1 s on the strict path, and any event carrying a ClockStamp is skew-checked (the live artifact agrees within 0.205 ms; a shifted-freshness relabel now refuses); claim-time rederivation authenticates the EXECUTED v3 schedule (pulse durations, the deterministic van-der-Corput gap sequence within ±0.25 s, ≥4.5 s commanded-quiet baselines) so phase-locked or degenerate captures cannot claim the 95/95 identity; and the canonical floor/MDE artifact carries the corner-widened floor additively (validator recomputes it; the analysis engine consumes the WIDENED guarded floor as operative) — closing the honest-artifact-fails-closed gap so a sound end-to-end floor/MDE handoff exists. Registry additions for this wave: <code>instrument_calibration_bracket_missing</code>, <code>calibration_bracket_exceeds_minted_bound</code>, (claim-bearing window not bracketed by two authenticated, fresh calibration artifacts, or bracket drift beyond the registered tolerance) and <code>thermal_pressure_elevated_in_window</code> (per-interval thermal-pressure records non-nominal — or missing on the strict path — anywhere in the admission-to-window span). Both only refuse; the PENDING_DECISION_LOG_REGISTRATION exception for them is retired with this entry.</p> <ol start="7"> <li><p><strong>Sign-off evidence must be head-minted.</strong> Any artifact or re-reduction quoted as validation evidence for a head must be regenerated AT that head (the pre-233e9e3 rederived calibration artifact lacks the horizon fields the head requires, and the probe re-reductions predate the strict calibration gates — both are re-minted at the final head before the sign-off record is written). Claim-bearing measurement additionally requires fresh live [QUIET-MAC] calibration under protocol v3 (59 pulses, fifth-wave addendum), bracketing the window, within 24 h of collection.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Confirmation round 9 (2026-07-22, FINAL under the Ed-ratified cap) — outcome and registered limitation L1.</strong> The round-9 review over head 040ca3a confirmed the fiducial chain, reduce-side verification taxonomy, and contract coherence clean, with ONE surviving blocker (CR9-1, repro-backed, lead-reproduced): the canonical floor/MDE artifact is SELF-ATTESTING about its admissible half-widths and campaign membership — <code>validate_floor_artifact</code> recomputes widened floors only from artifact-internal widths, and evidence binding authenticates identities, hashes, and ordering but neither rederives source widths nor requires complete governed campaign membership. A substituted artifact with understated widths (or one omitting a member) validates, binds, and licenses an exact claim floor. Per the loop-termination doctrine (clause 5), the lead adjudicates this a REGISTERED LIMITATION rather than a tenth round:</p> <ul> <li><strong>L1 (registered): canonical floor artifacts are not independently claim-licensing.</strong> Until floor↔extraction binding lands, a claim-bearing analysis may consume a floor artifact ONLY when it was produced by the governed extraction in the same custody session as the analysis (same run manifest; extraction gates demonstrably executed). Standalone or externally supplied floor artifacts are non-claim-bearing evidence. Justification: the exposure is artifact substitution or a defective producer BETWEEN extraction and analysis; an honest same-session pipeline computes widths and membership under the already -hardened extraction gates, so no measurement this program will make under L1&#39;s workflow rule is affected. The gap is a third-party verifiability deficit, not an instrument-physics defect.</li> <li><strong>Queued fix (next cycle, P1):</strong> bind each canonical floor cell to its extraction report and source-member disposition (or rederive the extraction gates and widths at binding), refusing on any stored width/corner mismatch or membership deviation, with integration regressions for width substitution and member omission (TASK_QUEUE FLOOR-BIND-01). Round-9 verification note: the focused 357-test review surface passed at the head in-session; the lead&#39;s full-suite gate over the identical tree content (2088 passed / 15 skipped / 1570 subtests / 0 failures) stands as the aggregate confirmation.</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><strong>Live collection arc (2026-07-22/23) — collection-path regressions, occurrence supersession, and basis-scoped verdicts.</strong> The first live Window-A members after sign-off exposed collection-path defects invisible to nine review rounds without hardware; each was fixed under the ratified contracts (PR #80 canonical-attempt promotion + sole-sampler gapless design; PR #81 idle-slice cursor after forensics proved the slicer&#39;s own parsing contaminated the admission interval at the real ~120 ms powermetrics cadence). Two doctrine amendments were then ruled by the lead when the whole-window verdict path contradicted operational guidance (both defaults preserved, both overrides explicit and auditable):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Occurrence supersession (amends the round-6 occurrence-count doctrine):</strong> duplicated member occurrences still REFUSE by default; a duplicate may resolve to the present bundle only when an explicit operator supersession artifact (append-only, hash-sealed, naming the superseded occurrence, quarantine destination, and reason — <code>--record-supersession</code>) exists; two present bundles always refuse.</li> <li><strong>Basis-scoped whole-window verdicts:</strong> latest-wins remains rejected (verdict-shopping prevention); every verdict records a canonical evaluation-basis hash (member occurrence set + calibration bracket set<ul> <li>policy) and binds only that basis; consumers match the claim&#39;s basis; legacy basis-less verdict rows never govern new claims. Diagnostic-cascade decoupling and whole-window waiver consumption landed in the same wave. Windows a5 (108 members) and prior attempts remain NON-claim-bearing as whole windows (true clock-anchor refusal on one member; NEG-8 end reference measured ~2 h post-collection failed the drift gate at 0.778 J — the instrument correctly refusing a stale bracket); their corpora stand as instrument-proving evidence. The next clean bracketed window is the first claim attempt.</li> </ul> </li> </ul> </li> <li><p><strong>NEG-8 drift-gate estimand ruling (2026-07-24; lead-ruled; RATIFIED in amended SCREEN+BUDGET form by the clause-10 addendum below — this original gross-only form was superseded the same day and never collected under).</strong> The whole-window drift adjudication proved the gate as previously implemented compared the two reference cells&#39; admissible envelopes at opposite corners (~0.9-1.5 J stacked) against an underived 0.05 J constant — structurally unpassable even for a physically perfect window (a8 measured point drift 0.006718 J over 2.96 h on ~38.5 J references). Ruling: the gate estimand is POINT DRIFT abs(end_point_gross − start_point_gross); the idle-subtracted point drift and the opposite-corner envelope statistic are recorded diagnostics, never gating (envelope stacking double-counts instrument uncertainty already composed into floor envelopes). The bound is DERIVED: a hash-sealed <code>joulewise.neg8_drift_bound.v1</code> artifact minted by governed CLI from a named settled-reference corpus (n&gt;=10, predeclared estimator <code>d054_point_contrast_guard_v1</code> = max(sample_range_j, t_{0.975,n-1}·s·sqrt(2))), consumed with full provenance in the verdict output. Registry addition: <code>neg8_drift_bound_underived</code> (fail-closed refusal whenever no valid governed bound artifact exists). Windows a6/a8 may be re-verdicted under the derived bound (with explicit waivers for aborted-member fragments); a5 and a7 remain refused on their genuine grounds.</p> </li> </ol> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum — debate and Ed ratification (2026-07-24).</strong> Per Ed&#39;s direction the ruling was formally debated with the peer model before ratification. The peer DISAGREED with the ruling as written on one structural point and was adjudicated correct: the point-drift statistic is the right estimand but an anomaly screen is not proof of stability — passing the gate must never erase observed drift from the claim error budget (consistent with the repo&#39;s own D-054/D-057 language). Ed RATIFIED the amended SCREEN + BUDGET design (the debate&#39;s option F, full variant, Ed explicitly directing the maximal build): per-claim-family point-drift screens (gross AND idle-subtracted, each with its own derived bound); per-family drift ALLOWANCES propagated additively into every floor/claim envelope of the window, never zero even on passing windows (allowance = max(observed excursion, derived repeatability bound)); replicated endpoint references (n=3 per endpoint, means with standard errors) and one midpoint reference prospectively, with the allowance taken over the maximum absolute excursion across sampled points; drift-bound artifacts carry a freshness horizon and re-derivation triggers (OS/build, power-supply, calibration-identity changes) with a distinct stale-bound refusal spelling; legacy pair-only windows evaluate under the single-member-endpoint minimum. Ed&#39;s recorded guardrails: watch the RIGOR SPIRAL (floors inflating past the effect sizes the science needs — monitor floor-vs-expected-effect at every extraction) and NO INVENTED PHYSICS (no functional form without a defensible basis; stated limitations beat unjustified formulas). Guiding light for all measurement-program decisions: the Splitwise replication (P2-006); methodology grounding against the Splitwise paper and comparable energy-measurement literature is in flight and feeds the collection design. Economics note recorded: Ed values artifact quality over time/tokens/machine-hours (project runs months ahead of deadline).</p> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum 2 — screen+budget wave registry + anchor-fallback gate ruling (lead, 2026-07-24).</strong> Registers the wave&#39;s spellings in the D-078 closed registry: <code>neg8_idle_sub_drift_bound_underived</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_idle_sub_abs_delta_exceeded</code>, and <code>neg8_drift_bound_stale</code> (freshness horizon exceeded or re-derivation trigger fired) — the ratified clause-10 design&#39;s concrete spellings — plus <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code> (unwaivable, no waiver spelling exists: a fallback-clock-anchored member may not anchor a floor or claim cell; in a floor cell it is an unwaivable re-run trigger). The latter is a LEAD-INITIATED ruling from the 2026-07-24 a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (<code>a7_vs_a5_prefill_scatter_analysis.md</code>): a7&#39;s 11.85 J prefill &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member (r03), half-width-zero envelope — instrument artifact (true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J). Flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review. Also registered (fix-round F3): <code>whole_window_drift_allowance_unrecorded</code> (passing basis-bearing verdict with no authenticated per-family allowance, or a claim missing its named allowance term — refuse, never zero; in both the floor-extraction and reducer vocabularies, mirroring <code>interpolation_bound_unrecorded</code>).</p> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum 3 — terminal mock bar (lead, 2026-07-24).</strong> The ratified premise &quot;mock telemetry can never bear claims&quot; had no terminal enforcement at the analysis claim boundary: honest mock members reached floor cells and claim evidence with the mock-exempted barriers disabled. Registered spelling: <code>mock_telemetry_claim_ineligible</code> (claim-bearing consumption of a member whose custody-bound config telemetry backend is the mock class; refuse — development-only evidence, no waiver spelling exists). Mockness derives from the custody-bound config (<code>hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bytes bound via <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>), never from summary/metadata labels alone; where such a config exists, config/metadata/summary telemetry identities must agree by backend class (governed <code>mock:*</code> tags are mock class) or the bundle is strict-invalid. Config absence is non-production evidence (fixture-only permissive paths keep their ratified intent). Lead-initiated; flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review.</p> <ol start="11"> <li><strong>Attribution-limited detection floors — Ed-RATIFIED amendment (2026-07-25).</strong> The first collection under the merged SCREEN+BUDGET rules (windows a9, a10; both whole-window verdicts PASSED) could not produce a floor: all three of a10&#39;s phase-absolute cells refuse <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code>. <strong>Finding: the instrument is ATTRIBUTION-limited, not NOISE-limited.</strong> Repeatability is 0.29-0.49 J on ~50 J points (and a settled reference pair three hours apart agreed to 0.007 J), but each member carries a clock-anchor-shift envelope of ~0.7-1.0 J: a +/-31 ms window shift across a phase boundary where power swings ~33 W mis-attributes ~1 J between prefill and decode. The composed bound is additive and measured — fiducial 24.9 ms (80-87%) plus bundle-local 3.3-6.1 ms plus edge span. Because repeatability will always beat attribution here, the refusal is STRUCTURALLY PERMANENT: no future phase corpus can pass it and there is nothing to re-collect around.</li> </ol> <p> <strong>Alternatives measured and eliminated</strong> (authenticated replay, 2026-07-25): (a) the calibration-bracket gap is NOT the cause — every cell refuses under both its minted and its post-bracket bound (delta +0.167 ms); (b) instrument tightening cannot rescue it — extraction would require a 10x (decode) to 32x (prefill) bound reduction, and each cell&#39;s bundle-local term ALONE (3.3-6.1 ms) already exceeds the entire required bound (0.99-2.9 ms), so even a perfect fiducial calibration would still refuse; (c) coarser granularity does not rescue it — request-level cells replayed on a10 and a8 have smaller envelopes (1.5-1.9 J) but still dominate and still refuse; (d) an ABBA common-mode estimator gives a real 3x gain (a5 decode 6.46 J -&gt; 2.13 J) but remains above that cell&#39;s 0.60 J point floor. The labelled path below is therefore not the preferred option among several — it is the only remaining path to any detection floor at all, at any granularity, on this instrument.</p> <p> <strong>Ruling (Ed-ratified).</strong> D-054 registers the detection floor as a practical prediction bound on FALSE OBSERVED EFFECTS, not as a repeatability statistic; a false observed effect may arise from scatter OR from anchor mis-attribution, and the corner-widened maximum is exactly the largest false effect this instrument can produce. <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code> therefore becomes a LABELLED CLAIM PATH rather than a hard refusal: extraction publishes the widened floor with a <code>floor_source</code> field naming the dominant term (here <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>) and retains the point floor separately as the repeatability diagnostic. The gate keeps its real function — preventing a repeatability-only number from publishing as if it were the whole story — while no longer conflating &quot;unsound corpus&quot; with &quot;instrument-limited floor&quot;. a10 is sound.</p> <p> <strong>Binding condition — SINGLE-COUNT DISCIPLINE (Ed: &quot;the cost seems sensible as long as it&#39;s noted&quot;).</strong> The floor gate now contains the anchor term, and each claim&#39;s decision interval separately consumes the member&#39;s <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>. These are different objects (calibration false-effect bound vs claim-side measurement uncertainty) and both are legitimate, but the consequence is that the effective clearable effect is FLOOR + CLAIM-SIDE BOUND (~5 J for phase contrasts), not the floor alone. Every artifact publishing an attribution-limited floor must state this explicitly so that neither term is later removed as an apparent double count. Science must be sized to the ~5 J bar; Splitwise-class effects (tens of percent of tens of joules) clear it with margin.</p> <p> <strong>Not authorised by this amendment:</strong> any instrument-tightening program. Revisit only if a pilot shows target effects below ~3x the widened floor. The free lever is workload sizing — attribution error is approximately duration-independent while effects scale with workload, so longer prefill/decode raises effect-to-floor linearly at zero instrument cost (queue FLOOR-WORKLOAD-SIZING-01).</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <strong aria-current="page">Recent</strong> · <a href="decision_log_archive_1.html">Archive 1</a></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

id="d-078-soundness-gate-no-claim-bearing-extraction-from-time-anchor-defective-powermetrics-corpora">D-078: Soundness gate — no claim-bearing extraction from time-anchor-defective powermetrics corpora</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-19. Owner: lead session under Ed&#39;s soundness-audit directive; recorded so the gate binds future sessions immediately. Status update 2026-07-22: the gate has been operative under Ed&#39;s direction through the entire repair arc, and Ed explicitly ratified the close-out cap (clause 8); formal ratification of this original text rides the PR #79 review (Ed may amend).</p> <p>The 2026-07-19 measurement-soundness audit (<code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>; all P0 findings lead-verified from primary evidence) found that powermetrics trace timestamps are misaligned with runtime events at the ~0.5–1 s scale (pre-spawn/first-parse midpoint anchor), making request/phase/item point energies physically non-attributable as recorded across ALL existing powermetrics corpora, including the 2026-07-17 published floor extraction.</p> <p>Binding until amended:</p> <ol> <li>No claim-bearing floor, MDE, or L2/L3 energy claim may be published from any corpus collected under the defective anchor. Existing corpora are instrument/calibration evidence only.</li> <li>Extraction must treat <code>window_evidence_precheck</code> as a hard gate and must join campaign-log cooldown/admission evidence (cap hits are not clean n). &quot;Claim-eligible&quot; narrative language may describe METRIC-level eligibility only, never source provenance alone.</li> <li>The repair path (roadmap Phase 0, <code>docs/phase_2/splitwise_replication_roadmap.md</code>): tight causal anchor + anchor-shift joule envelope in reduction, analysis-engine 0.5.0/v2 wire compat, CPU-aware idle admission, prospective NEG-8 acceptance threshold. Stored summaries are never rewritten; fixes are prospective.</li> <li>The 2026-07-17 published floor table is caveated in PROJECT_STATUS pending re-extraction; advisor-brief/site correction timing is Ed&#39;s deployment decision (D-068).</li> </ol> <p>Revisit trigger: Phase 0 repair lands with live pulse-validation evidence, or Ed rules a different salvage/disposition for existing corpora.</p> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-20: fail-closed vocabulary and immutable summaries</h3> <p>Additive amendment under the adversarial soundness fix round. The following spellings are the binding, closed registry for D-078 claim refusals and campaign conditions.
