Stored summary bytes are now immutable evidence. Post-hoc reduction writes a new, non-clobbering artifact (including the repaired anchor envelope) or refuses; the raw-artifact immutability and pure-reducer portions of D-002/D-028 remain in force. Frozen 0.5.0/0.6.0 numeric semantics remain replayable and are not claim-bearing merely because they can be read.</p> <h3>D-078 additive registry addendum — 2026-07-20: causal-set repair</h3> <p>The closed registry additionally includes floor/whole-window barriers <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code>, <code>whole_window_verdict_coverage_incomplete</code>, <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code>, and <code>whole_window_verdict_conflict</code>. Instrument-evidence diagnostics additionally include <code>no_plateau_interior_intervals</code>, <code>plateau_below_minimum</code>, <code>robust_snr_below_minimum</code>, <code>edge_coverage_missing</code>, <code>model_fit_not_significant</code>, and <code>fitted_shift_exceeds_validation_limit</code>. These additions only refuse or widen uncertainty; none can license a claim.</p> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-21: convergence fix wave (lead adjudications)</h3> <p>Recorded by the lead after the two-round cross-model convergence loop over <code>impl/p0-instrument-repair</code> (round-2 and round-3 fix waves; council log carries the layer accounting). Six rulings:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Additive causal-bound composition.</strong> <code>B_effective = B_bundle + B_fiducial</code> replaces <code>max(B_bundle, B_fiducial)</code>. The bundle-local censored-constraint anchor interval and the instrument&#39;s emission-lag bound sit on disjoint causal links; no containment proof exists, so <code>max()</code> under-composes. <code>B_fiducial</code> itself additively folds in the calibration capture&#39;s own trace-anchor bound. The prior <code>max()</code> text in this log is superseded prospectively; stored summaries are never rewritten.</li> <li><strong>Identity bump, not in-place semantics change.</strong> The additive composition, fiducial protocol_v2 physics (<code>joint_loss_sublevel_interval_branch_v2</code> full 2-D branch-and-bound region), and the stricter evidence-admission semantics are minted as reducer <code>0.5.2</code> / AXI <code>0.6.2</code> with <code>configs/calibration/powermetrics_fiducial/protocol_v2.json</code>. <code>0.5.1</code> / <code>0.6.1</code> and <code>protocol_v1.json</code> remain byte-frozen replay arms.</li> <li><strong>Superseded arms are claim-ineligible.</strong> <code>0.5.1</code>/<code>0.6.1</code> summaries refuse claim-bearing use with a registered refusal (superseded max-composition envelope semantics); <code>0.5.2</code>/<code>0.6.2</code> are the sole claim-eligible mints.</li> <li><strong>Registry additions (closing the F11/PENDING exception).</strong> The closed refusal vocabulary additionally includes <code>token_count_stream_chunk_fallback</code> (renamed from the source-label reuse of <code>stream_chunk_fallback</code>), <code>pulse_calibration_rollover_gate_timeout</code> (pre-workload rollover gate timeout now refuses fail-closed, no artifact minting), and <code>post_window_trace_tail_shorter_than_anchor_bound</code> (reduce-time refusal when the post-window trace tail cannot support the composed anchor bound; collection policy raises the minimum post-window dwell to 1.0 s). These only refuse; none can license a claim.</li> <li><strong>Registry closure is one-way by design.</strong> Every emitted spelling must be registered here; a registered spelling with no current emission site (e.g. <code>window_evidence_precheck_failed</code>, <code>cap_hit_drift_term_unavailable</code>) is permitted — unemittable names cannot launder anything.</li> <li><strong>Member-level <code>claim_evidence_flags</code> is an all-leaf union — documented, not changed.</strong> Adjudicated a documentation defect only: the union is fail-safe (it can only over-flag, never over-admit) and gating decisions read the per-metric leaves. Scope documented in <code>docs/contracts/run_bundle_layout.md</code>; no wire rename.</li> </ol> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-21 (second): two-edge envelope and confirmation-round rulings</h3> <p>Recorded by the lead after the first confirmation round over <code>5093355</code> correctly withheld sign-off (fresh Sol xhigh audit; 8 confirmed findings, one P0). Rulings:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Corner-composed two-edge envelope (P0 repair).</strong> The calibration fits independent start-edge and stop-edge emission lags; a single common trace shift under-covers because independent endpoint errors move energy by up to <code>2·P·B_fiducial</code> even when a common shift cancels. The claim envelope is now the extrema over start = <code>delta_common + eps_on</code>, stop = <code>delta_common + eps_off</code> with <code>|delta_common| &lt;= B_bundle</code> and <code>|eps_on|, |eps_off| &lt;= B_fiducial</code> independent. For nonnegative power the energy is monotone in each edge separately, so exact extrema are attained at the four edge corners with the common shift scanned continuously — the existing breakpoint-exact scan run per corner. The per-edge corner offset is <code>±(B_fiducial + wall_minus_monotonic_span)</code>: the span is a third disjoint per-edge error source, folded into the corners (delta-review amendment) rather than the frozen arms&#39; cruder <code>2·span·maxP</code> additive term, and the composed <code>anchor_bound_s</code> = <code>B_bundle + B_fiducial + span</code> governs the tail-sufficiency gate identically. Idle-subtracted and per-token envelopes additionally widen by <code>2·(B_fiducial + span)·P_idle</code> because independent edges vary the subtracted idle duration (delta re-audit catch). New registered method spelling for the 0.5.2/0.6.2 mints; v1/v2 spellings remain replay-read-only.</li> <li><strong>In-place revision of the unreleased mints.</strong> Reducer 0.5.2 / AXI 0.6.2 were never merged or used for stored artifacts; their envelope semantics are revised in place (no 0.5.3/0.6.3 inflation). Goldens regenerated and hand-verified against the formula.</li> <li><strong>Registry additions.</strong> The closed refusal vocabulary additionally includes <code>negative_power_sample</code> (negative rail power reaching the envelope/energy path breaks the monotonicity argument and refuses fail-closed) and <code>instrument_calibration_stale</code> (calibration artifacts now record capture wall time and a 24 h <code>max_age_s</code> validity horizon in protocol_v2; claim-time verification refuses missing/invalid capture time or age exceeded — a finite 40-pulse residual maximum is not an out-of-sample bound without recency enforcement). Instrument-evidence diagnostics additionally include <code>capture_time_missing_or_invalid</code> (a v2 capture without a valid recorded capture wall time is invalid at minting, with the reason stated rather than silent). All only refuse; the PENDING_DECISION_LOG_REGISTRATION exception is retired with this entry. Replay purity note: the 0.5.1/0.6.1 arms keep their frozen binding expectation against the protocol_v2.json bytes current at their mint (<code>REPLAY_PROTOCOL_V2_SHA256</code>); custody-manifest verification and the staleness horizon are current-mint gates only.</li> <li><strong>Environment admission consumes the full evidence object.</strong> The shared validator fails closed on <code>critical_environment_passed</code>, <code>reference_provenance_present</code>, per-run evaluation eligibility, guard observations, and schema identity — and the post-run environment observation passes through the failure predicate on claim/whole-window paths (a post-run critical-environment failure refuses claim eligibility). This closes the Window-A screensaver contamination class end-to-end.</li> <li><strong>Calibration custody verified at claim time.</strong> The reducer enforces the validation-manifest reference: in-bundle containment, manifest hash, and presence + sha256 of every manifest member; any failure refuses as <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>. Current-era (0.5.2/0.6.2) claim-bearing use requires a protocol_v2 calibration artifact.</li> <li><strong>Collection floors.</strong> The 1.0 s post-window dwell minimum is enforced on every collection path (controller default, schema minimum, campaign-policy validation); sub-minimum configs refuse at validation. Scope spelling (delta-review adjudication): controller/CLI pre-collection rejection applies wherever powermetrics telemetry collects; mock-backend runs are not dwell-gated at the controller (mock telemetry cannot reach any claim path), while the campaign-policy schema minimum applies universally. Inner phase/item/block/level window entries carry the whole-trace anchor/calibration/tail barrier stamps whenever the top-level barrier fires.</li> <li><strong>Cooldown terminal-evidence normativity documented.</strong> The required terminal JSONL row fields (<code>release</code>, <code>release_criteria_met_late</code>), the cap-first precedence rule (&quot;the cap is causal and wins&quot;), and rejection semantics are contract text in <code>docs/contracts/run_bundle_layout.md</code>, matching <code>joulewise/cooldown.py</code> exactly.</li> </ol> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-21 (third): provenance authentication rulings</h3> <p>Recorded by the lead after confirmation round 2 over <code>233e9e3</code> withheld sign-off (9 confirmed; the physics verified clean from every lens — all findings are provenance/governance). Rulings, implemented in the round-3 fix wave (frozen 0.5.1/0.6.1 replay semantics unchanged throughout):</p> <ol> <li><strong>Declared facts are authenticated against primary bytes.</strong> The calibration&#39;s declared <code>capture_wall_time_s</code> must agree (±1 s) with the capture time independently derived from the hash-verified source events — a stale calibration can no longer be relabeled fresh (the P0).</li> <li><strong>Freshness covers the whole measurement.</strong> The 24 h horizon binds both <code>run_started</code> and the measured window END: <code>capture &lt;= run_started</code> and <code>window_end &lt;= capture + max_age_s</code>, inclusive. Pre-run delays cannot carry sampling past the declared validity of its calibration.</li> <li><strong>Version identity is validated generically.</strong> Generic bundle validation checks <code>reducer_version</code> against the closed known set and the §8.1 version/event-semantics pairing rules as a validation-time structured problem (no wire-schema enum — frozen-arm byte replay preserved); an unsupported <code>--reducer-version</code> yields the standard structured refusal, never a traceback.</li> <li><strong>Stored verdicts are re-derived, never trusted.</strong> The whole-window verifier rejects duplicated NEG-8 core members (occurrence-count semantics) and re-derives the bracket verdict from member evidence; disagreement with the stored row is <code>whole_window_verdict_conflict</code>. Delta-review strengthening (lead ruling): the re-derivation tolerances come from the repo-REGISTERED campaign policy whose file hash matches the row&#39;s <code>policy_sha256</code> — the one trust anchor that does not terminate at bundle custody. Unknown policy hashes, and rows whose self-asserted tolerances disagree with the registered policy, refuse <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> before re-derivation. The custody boundary is otherwise explicit: a forger with bundle write access can rewrite row-internal hashes consistently, but cannot mint a matching tracked policy file.</li> <li><strong>Protocol identity is shape-authenticated.</strong> A v2 <code>protocol_id</code> requires the v2 estimator identity, capture/horizon fields, and v2 residual shape; v1-shaped bodies relabeled v2 refuse <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>.</li> <li><strong>Admission attempts have timing semantics.</strong> Attempt-ledger rows carry strictly increasing, non-overlapping declared windows on the strict path; violations refuse <code>environment_admission_missing</code>. 7a. <strong>(Fourth-wave addendum — claim-aggregation rulings, same date.)</strong> After confirmation round 3 over <code>0925480</code> (instrument core verified defensible on fresh head collections by every lens; all four P0s in the claim-aggregation layer), the lead ruled: (1) floors/MDEs widen by EXACT linear-corner evaluation over member envelope intervals — residual widening <code>w_i·(n−1)/n + Σ_{j≠i}w_j/n</code>, contrast widening <code>Σ|c_i|·w_i</code> — never a max-width shortcut, and the dominance refusal fires against the widened quantity; (2) admission is causally bound to its run: the final attempt window ends at-or-before window start within <code>MAX_ADMISSION_GAP_S = 600</code> (inclusive), the post-run observation is captured at-or-after window end, and attempt windows must contain their stage&#39;s recorded idle-capture interval; (3) the whole-window verifier re-derives CPU admission and adapter continuity from member-bundle primary evidence, refuses nonempty condition lists and undecodable log lines (laundering must require consistent cross-bundle forgery, never a one-line edit — full erasure resistance inside bundle custody is impossible and is recorded as the honest boundary); (4) NEG-8 reference energies are re-reduced from primary evidence at the current mint at claim time (minutes-scale cost accepted), with canonical-workload identity (<code>canonical_neg8_workload</code> + <code>scientific_config_sha256</code> against the custody-bound config) enforced; (5) the four byte-frozen goldens carry executable sha256 pins. Round-4 confirmation follow-ups (same date): the universal <code>clock_anchor_unresolved</code> barrier covers the <code>0.4.1</code>/<code>0.4.2</code> arms (every pre-repair wire, not only 0.5.0/0.6.0 — the former 0.4.x escape is closed and its test assertion inverted); the production trace-margin gate uses the full three-term composed bound including the wall-minus-monotonic span; campaign <code>ready_for_analysis</code> requires a registered claim-eligible mint (<code>0.5.2</code>/<code>0.6.2</code>; mock telemetry exempt — it can never bear claims). Recorded custody boundary: the 24 h calibration horizon compares host wall time, so an operator with host time control can evade it — accepted (host time integrity is an operator obligation, like bundle custody itself).</li> </ol> <p>7b. <strong>(Fifth-wave addendum — calibration epistemics, same date.)</strong> After confirmation round 5 over <code>09b5de6</code> (the P0 was statistical, not mechanical: a 40-pulse sample maximum is not an out-of-sample deterministic bound — 87.1% confidence on the 95th percentile vs the D-054 doctrine&#39;s n=59 for 95/95), the lead ruled: (1) <strong>protocol_v3</strong> raises the pulse count to 59, satisfying the repo&#39;s own nonparametric 95/95 doctrine; v3 is required for future claim-bearing calibration captures (v2 artifacts stay verifiable as this arc&#39;s validation evidence). (2) <strong>B_fiducial&#39;s epistemic status is stated honestly everywhere</strong>: a 95/95 nonparametric calibration bound, deterministic for claims only under REGISTERED transfer assumptions — T1 binding-vector stationarity, T2 the authenticated 24 h horizon, T3 load-regime transfer (calibration pulses are GPU-matmul under CPU-light load; sustained mixed-load transfer is an assumption; a loaded-calibration protocol variant is the registered roadmap mitigation). (3) <strong>Calibration bracketing is required for claim-bearing collections</strong>: two valid artifacts bracketing the window (pre at-or-before start, post at-or-after end, each within its own horizon), consumed as <code>max(pre, post)</code>, refusing <code>instrument_calibration_bracket_missing</code> or on bracket drift beyond <code>calibration_bracket_max_drift_s</code> (production 10 ms). Single-calibration reduction remains valid only for non-claim-bearing probe/exploratory use. (4) <strong>Environment state is window-enforced</strong>: per-interval thermal-pressure records are scanned over the measured window (<code>thermal_pressure_elevated_in_window</code> refusal); admission objects are recomputed from their embedded snapshots — a stored <code>eligible: true</code> is never trusted. (5) <strong>Loop-termination doctrine</strong>: convergence sign-off means zero UNADDRESSED P0/P1, where &quot;addressed&quot; includes a registered limitation with recorded justification, adjudicated by the lead. A physical instrument&#39;s uncertainty budget always rests on stated assumptions; the honest end state is registered assumptions, not infinite hardening. T3 is the first entry in that register. Round-6 follow-up (same date): the bracket maximum must be CONSUMED, not merely recorded — a claim refuses <code>calibration_bracket_exceeds_minted_bound</code> whenever <code>max(B_pre, B_post)</code> exceeds any member envelope&#39;s minted effective bound (the member must be re-reduced under the dominating calibration); the whole-window producer refuses duplicated member occurrences (occurrence-count doctrine at the producer, not just the claim verifier); the registered-policy trust anchor refuses duplicate-JSON-key policy bytes; and the standalone reducer horizon predicate upper-bounds <code>run_started</code> as well as the window end. Round-7 follow-ups (same date): the operative floor is the EXACT maximum of the complete D-054 guarded floor over the joint per-member interval corners (every component is convex in the member vector, so vertex enumeration is exact; n &lt;= 16 enumerated, larger widths refuse) — the linear-corner residual widening alone under-covered the Student-t prediction component; claim-licensing whole-window evidence requires the registered policy to be production-profile AND claim-bearing (exploratory rows can never license claims); the bracket-dominance gate authenticates each member&#39;s consumed bound from hash-verified calibration evidence (never the mint-time metadata scalar, whose disagreement is itself provenance-invalid); claim brackets accept protocol v3 artifacts ONLY (v2 stays valid as reduction/validation evidence). Round-8 follow-ups (2026-07-22): calibration identity is SEMANTICALLY authenticated, not just byte-authenticated — every calibration command event&#39;s two clocks (top-level <code>timestamp_s</code> and embedded ClockStamp epoch) must agree within 1 s on the strict path, and any event carrying a ClockStamp is skew-checked (the live artifact agrees within 0.205 ms; a shifted-freshness relabel now refuses); claim-time rederivation authenticates the EXECUTED v3 schedule (pulse durations, the deterministic van-der-Corput gap sequence within ±0.25 s, ≥4.5 s commanded-quiet baselines) so phase-locked or degenerate captures cannot claim the 95/95 identity; and the canonical floor/MDE artifact carries the corner-widened floor additively (validator recomputes it; the analysis engine consumes the WIDENED guarded floor as operative) — closing the honest-artifact-fails-closed gap so a sound end-to-end floor/MDE handoff exists. Registry additions for this wave: <code>instrument_calibration_bracket_missing</code>, <code>calibration_bracket_exceeds_minted_bound</code>, (claim-bearing window not bracketed by two authenticated, fresh calibration artifacts, or bracket drift beyond the registered tolerance) and <code>thermal_pressure_elevated_in_window</code> (per-interval thermal-pressure records non-nominal — or missing on the strict path — anywhere in the admission-to-window span). Both only refuse; the PENDING_DECISION_LOG_REGISTRATION exception for them is retired with this entry.</p> <ol start="7"> <li><p><strong>Sign-off evidence must be head-minted.</strong> Any artifact or re-reduction quoted as validation evidence for a head must be regenerated AT that head (the pre-233e9e3 rederived calibration artifact lacks the horizon fields the head requires, and the probe re-reductions predate the strict calibration gates — both are re-minted at the final head before the sign-off record is written). Claim-bearing measurement additionally requires fresh live [QUIET-MAC] calibration under protocol v3 (59 pulses, fifth-wave addendum), bracketing the window, within 24 h of collection.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Confirmation round 9 (2026-07-22, FINAL under the Ed-ratified cap) — outcome and registered limitation L1.</strong> The round-9 review over head 040ca3a confirmed the fiducial chain, reduce-side verification taxonomy, and contract coherence clean, with ONE surviving blocker (CR9-1, repro-backed, lead-reproduced): the canonical floor/MDE artifact is SELF-ATTESTING about its admissible half-widths and campaign membership — <code>validate_floor_artifact</code> recomputes widened floors only from artifact-internal widths, and evidence binding authenticates identities, hashes, and ordering but neither rederives source widths nor requires complete governed campaign membership. A substituted artifact with understated widths (or one omitting a member) validates, binds, and licenses an exact claim floor. Per the loop-termination doctrine (clause 5), the lead adjudicates this a REGISTERED LIMITATION rather than a tenth round:</p> <ul> <li><strong>L1 (registered): canonical floor artifacts are not independently claim-licensing.</strong> Until floor↔extraction binding lands, a claim-bearing analysis may consume a floor artifact ONLY when it was produced by the governed extraction in the same custody session as the analysis (same run manifest; extraction gates demonstrably executed). Standalone or externally supplied floor artifacts are non-claim-bearing evidence. Justification: the exposure is artifact substitution or a defective producer BETWEEN extraction and analysis; an honest same-session pipeline computes widths and membership under the already -hardened extraction gates, so no measurement this program will make under L1&#39;s workflow rule is affected. The gap is a third-party verifiability deficit, not an instrument-physics defect.</li> <li><strong>Queued fix (next cycle, P1):</strong> bind each canonical floor cell to its extraction report and source-member disposition (or rederive the extraction gates and widths at binding), refusing on any stored width/corner mismatch or membership deviation, with integration regressions for width substitution and member omission (TASK_QUEUE FLOOR-BIND-01). Round-9 verification note: the focused 357-test review surface passed at the head in-session; the lead&#39;s full-suite gate over the identical tree content (2088 passed / 15 skipped / 1570 subtests / 0 failures) stands as the aggregate confirmation.</li> </ul> </li> <li><p><strong>Live collection arc (2026-07-22/23) — collection-path regressions, occurrence supersession, and basis-scoped verdicts.</strong> The first live Window-A members after sign-off exposed collection-path defects invisible to nine review rounds without hardware; each was fixed under the ratified contracts (PR #80 canonical-attempt promotion + sole-sampler gapless design; PR #81 idle-slice cursor after forensics proved the slicer&#39;s own parsing contaminated the admission interval at the real ~120 ms powermetrics cadence). Two doctrine amendments were then ruled by the lead when the whole-window verdict path contradicted operational guidance (both defaults preserved, both overrides explicit and auditable):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Occurrence supersession (amends the round-6 occurrence-count doctrine):</strong> duplicated member occurrences still REFUSE by default; a duplicate may resolve to the present bundle only when an explicit operator supersession artifact (append-only, hash-sealed, naming the superseded occurrence, quarantine destination, and reason — <code>--record-supersession</code>) exists; two present bundles always refuse.</li> <li><strong>Basis-scoped whole-window verdicts:</strong> latest-wins remains rejected (verdict-shopping prevention); every verdict records a canonical evaluation-basis hash (member occurrence set + calibration bracket set<ul> <li>policy) and binds only that basis; consumers match the claim&#39;s basis; legacy basis-less verdict rows never govern new claims. Diagnostic-cascade decoupling and whole-window waiver consumption landed in the same wave. Windows a5 (108 members) and prior attempts remain NON-claim-bearing as whole windows (true clock-anchor refusal on one member; NEG-8 end reference measured ~2 h post-collection failed the drift gate at 0.778 J — the instrument correctly refusing a stale bracket); their corpora stand as instrument-proving evidence. The next clean bracketed window is the first claim attempt.</li> </ul> </li> </ul> </li> <li><p><strong>NEG-8 drift-gate estimand ruling (2026-07-24; lead-ruled; RATIFIED in amended SCREEN+BUDGET form by the clause-10 addendum below — this original gross-only form was superseded the same day and never collected under).</strong> The whole-window drift adjudication proved the gate as previously implemented compared the two reference cells&#39; admissible envelopes at opposite corners (~0.9-1.5 J stacked) against an underived 0.05 J constant — structurally unpassable even for a physically perfect window (a8 measured point drift 0.006718 J over 2.96 h on ~38.5 J references). Ruling: the gate estimand is POINT DRIFT abs(end_point_gross − start_point_gross); the idle-subtracted point drift and the opposite-corner envelope statistic are recorded diagnostics, never gating (envelope stacking double-counts instrument uncertainty already composed into floor envelopes). The bound is DERIVED: a hash-sealed <code>joulewise.neg8_drift_bound.v1</code> artifact minted by governed CLI from a named settled-reference corpus (n&gt;=10, predeclared estimator <code>d054_point_contrast_guard_v1</code> = max(sample_range_j, t_{0.975,n-1}·s·sqrt(2))), consumed with full provenance in the verdict output. Registry addition: <code>neg8_drift_bound_underived</code> (fail-closed refusal whenever no valid governed bound artifact exists). Windows a6/a8 may be re-verdicted under the derived bound (with explicit waivers for aborted-member fragments); a5 and a7 remain refused on their genuine grounds.</p> </li> </ol> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum — debate and Ed ratification (2026-07-24).</strong> Per Ed&#39;s direction the ruling was formally debated with the peer model before ratification. The peer DISAGREED with the ruling as written on one structural point and was adjudicated correct: the point-drift statistic is the right estimand but an anomaly screen is not proof of stability — passing the gate must never erase observed drift from the claim error budget (consistent with the repo&#39;s own D-054/D-057 language). Ed RATIFIED the amended SCREEN + BUDGET design (the debate&#39;s option F, full variant, Ed explicitly directing the maximal build): per-claim-family point-drift screens (gross AND idle-subtracted, each with its own derived bound); per-family drift ALLOWANCES propagated additively into every floor/claim envelope of the window, never zero even on passing windows (allowance = max(observed excursion, derived repeatability bound)); replicated endpoint references (n=3 per endpoint, means with standard errors) and one midpoint reference prospectively, with the allowance taken over the maximum absolute excursion across sampled points; drift-bound artifacts carry a freshness horizon and re-derivation triggers (OS/build, power-supply, calibration-identity changes) with a distinct stale-bound refusal spelling; legacy pair-only windows evaluate under the single-member-endpoint minimum. Ed&#39;s recorded guardrails: watch the RIGOR SPIRAL (floors inflating past the effect sizes the science needs — monitor floor-vs-expected-effect at every extraction) and NO INVENTED PHYSICS (no functional form without a defensible basis; stated limitations beat unjustified formulas). Guiding light for all measurement-program decisions: the Splitwise replication (P2-006); methodology grounding against the Splitwise paper and comparable energy-measurement literature is in flight and feeds the collection design. Economics note recorded: Ed values artifact quality over time/tokens/machine-hours (project runs months ahead of deadline).</p> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum 2 — screen+budget wave registry + anchor-fallback gate ruling (lead, 2026-07-24).</strong> Registers the wave&#39;s spellings in the D-078 closed registry: <code>neg8_idle_sub_drift_bound_underived</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_idle_sub_abs_delta_exceeded</code>, and <code>neg8_drift_bound_stale</code> (freshness horizon exceeded or re-derivation trigger fired) — the ratified clause-10 design&#39;s concrete spellings — plus <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code> (unwaivable, no waiver spelling exists: a fallback-clock-anchored member may not anchor a floor or claim cell; in a floor cell it is an unwaivable re-run trigger). The latter is a LEAD-INITIATED ruling from the 2026-07-24 a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (<code>a7_vs_a5_prefill_scatter_analysis.md</code>): a7&#39;s 11.85 J prefill &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member (r03), half-width-zero envelope — instrument artifact (true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J). Flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review. Also registered (fix-round F3): <code>whole_window_drift_allowance_unrecorded</code> (passing basis-bearing verdict with no authenticated per-family allowance, or a claim missing its named allowance term — refuse, never zero; in both the floor-extraction and reducer vocabularies, mirroring <code>interpolation_bound_unrecorded</code>).</p> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum 3 — terminal mock bar (lead, 2026-07-24).</strong> The ratified premise &quot;mock telemetry can never bear claims&quot; had no terminal enforcement at the analysis claim boundary: honest mock members reached floor cells and claim evidence with the mock-exempted barriers disabled. Registered spelling: <code>mock_telemetry_claim_ineligible</code> (claim-bearing consumption of a member whose custody-bound config telemetry backend is the mock class; refuse — development-only evidence, no waiver spelling exists). Mockness derives from the custody-bound config (<code>hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bytes bound via <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>), never from summary/metadata labels alone; where such a config exists, config/metadata/summary telemetry identities must agree by backend class (governed <code>mock:*</code> tags are mock class) or the bundle is strict-invalid. Config absence is non-production evidence (fixture-only permissive paths keep their ratified intent). Lead-initiated; flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review.</p> <ol start="11"> <li><strong>Attribution-limited detection floors — Ed-RATIFIED amendment (2026-07-25).</strong> The first collection under the merged SCREEN+BUDGET rules (windows a9, a10; both whole-window verdicts PASSED) could not produce a floor: all three of a10&#39;s phase-absolute cells refuse <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code>. <strong>Finding: the instrument is ATTRIBUTION-limited, not NOISE-limited.</strong> Repeatability is 0.29-0.49 J on ~50 J points (and a settled reference pair three hours apart agreed to 0.007 J), but each member carries a clock-anchor-shift envelope of ~0.7-1.0 J: a +/-31 ms window shift across a phase boundary where power swings ~33 W mis-attributes ~1 J between prefill and decode. The composed bound is additive and measured — fiducial 24.9 ms (80-87%) plus bundle-local 3.3-6.1 ms plus edge span. Because repeatability will always beat attribution here, the refusal is STRUCTURALLY PERMANENT: no future phase corpus can pass it and there is nothing to re-collect around.</li> </ol> <p> <strong>Alternatives measured and eliminated</strong> (authenticated replay, 2026-07-25): (a) the calibration-bracket gap is NOT the cause — every cell refuses under both its minted and its post-bracket bound (delta +0.167 ms); (b) instrument tightening cannot rescue it — extraction would require a 10x (decode) to 32x (prefill) bound reduction, and each cell&#39;s bundle-local term ALONE (3.3-6.1 ms) already exceeds the entire required bound (0.99-2.9 ms), so even a perfect fiducial calibration would still refuse; (c) coarser granularity does not rescue it — request-level cells replayed on a10 and a8 have smaller envelopes (1.5-1.9 J) but still dominate and still refuse; (d) an ABBA common-mode estimator gives a real 3x gain (a5 decode 6.46 J -&gt; 2.13 J) but remains above that cell&#39;s 0.60 J point floor. The labelled path below is therefore not the preferred option among several — it is the only remaining path to any detection floor at all, at any granularity, on this instrument.</p> <p> <strong>Ruling (Ed-ratified).</strong> D-054 registers the detection floor as a practical prediction bound on FALSE OBSERVED EFFECTS, not as a repeatability statistic; a false observed effect may arise from scatter OR from anchor mis-attribution, and the corner-widened maximum is exactly the largest false effect this instrument can produce. <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code> therefore becomes a LABELLED CLAIM PATH rather than a hard refusal: extraction publishes the widened floor with a <code>floor_source</code> field naming the dominant term (here <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>) and retains the point floor separately as the repeatability diagnostic. The gate keeps its real function — preventing a repeatability-only number from publishing as if it were the whole story — while no longer conflating &quot;unsound corpus&quot; with &quot;instrument-limited floor&quot;. a10 is sound.</p> <p> <strong>Binding condition — SINGLE-COUNT DISCIPLINE (Ed: &quot;the cost seems sensible as long as it&#39;s noted&quot;).</strong> The floor gate now contains the anchor term, and each claim&#39;s decision interval separately consumes the member&#39;s <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>. These are different objects (calibration false-effect bound vs claim-side measurement uncertainty) and both are legitimate, but the consequence is that the effective clearable effect is FLOOR + CLAIM-SIDE BOUND (~5 J for phase contrasts), not the floor alone. Every artifact publishing an attribution-limited floor must state this explicitly so that neither term is later removed as an apparent double count. Science must be sized to the ~5 J bar; Splitwise-class effects (tens of percent of tens of joules) clear it with margin.</p> <p> <strong>Not authorised by this amendment:</strong> any instrument-tightening program. Revisit only if a pilot shows target effects below ~3x the widened floor. The free lever is workload sizing — attribution error is approximately duration-independent while effects scale with workload, so longer prefill/decode raises effect-to-floor linearly at zero instrument cost (queue FLOOR-WORKLOAD-SIZING-01).</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <strong aria-current="page">Recent</strong> · <a href="decision_log_archive_1.html">Archive 1</a></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-night-hardening/AUDIT-LEDGER.md:11107:docs/site/adapter_contracts.html:48:</code></pre> <p>Only the reducer may assign <code>below_floor</code>; <code>excluded_from_claim</code> is analysis-only and invalid in runtime events or summaries (D-045.4).</p> <p>Prompt-source handling is per item and mutually exclusive. <code>prompt_text</code> is encoded at generation time with adapter-normal special-token behavior (MLX uses <code>add_special_tokens=True</code>, so BOS is inside the planned prompt budget). <code>prompt_token_ids</code> is ids-native and delivered exactly as listed, with no BOS added; this is required for D-046 sentinel conditions. Absent text and ids use a synthetic prompt with <code>shape.planned_prompt_tokens</code>. Any field named <code>prompt_sha256</code> means the domain-separated token-ID hash, not a text hash.</p> <p>For prompt-text items with a SHA-256-shaped <code>source.source_sha256</code>, runtimes compare the realized prompt token-ID hash against <code>source_sha256</code>; if it does not match, they may accept <code>sha256(prompt_text)</code> as a text-domain manifest. Any other value fails the item closed as <code>malformed</code> with <code>status_reason: &quot;prompt_ids_mismatch&quot;</code>. For planned prompt token counts, <code>jw_mixed_v1</code> prompt-text items are budgeted and a realized/planned mismatch is fatal; affine ladder prompt-text items are nominal and receive an advisory annotation instead.</p> <p><code>suite_items.jsonl.prompt_source</code> is one of <code>prompt_text</code>, <code>token_ids</code>, or <code>synthetic</code>. <code>bos_present</code> records whether BOS is present in the realized prompt. For text-path adapters, when the tokenizer exposes a BOS id this is <code>add_special_tokens=True</code> and first realized id equals the tokenizer BOS id; when the tokenizer does not expose BOS identity, <code>bos_present</code> records the honest encode-mode proxy (<code>add_special_tokens=True</code>). Ids-native and synthetic suite prompts record <code>false</code> unless a future adapter explicitly materializes BOS as part of those sources.</p> <h2 id="telemetry-adapter">Telemetry Adapter</h2> <p>Telemetry answers how power and thermal state are measured.</p> <p>Required behavior:</p> <ul> <li>Report device metadata, including the rail manifest: the exact rail names whose per-timestamp sum defines the backend&#39;s canonical <code>power_w</code> (D-018). Rail manifest entries are strings; non-string entries are rejected by the bundle reader rather than coerced.</li> <li>Measure idle baseline.</li> <li>Start power sampling.</li> <li>Stop power sampling.</li> <li>Emit raw power samples.</li> <li>Report thermal state when available.</li> <li>Return structured failure if telemetry permission is missing.</li> </ul> <p>Rail-row timestamp contract (D-027, Slice 2N.4): one sample instant is one clock read, fanned out to one row per manifest rail, all carrying that instant&#39;s single <code>timestamp_s</code>. A manifest rail may appear at most once for a given timestamp; duplicate <code>(timestamp_s, rail)</code> rows are invalid, including single-rail manifests. With a multi-rail manifest, a timestamp carrying only a subset of the manifest rails is a misalignment: the shared bundle reader raises a structured failure (the reducer reports FAILED; the report omits the chart) and default bundle validation reports the same trace-policy problem rather than silently producing an interleaved, undersummed, or double-counted curve. An adapter whose hardware samples rails at genuinely different instants must resample/align to shared timestamps before emitting rows - alignment policy belongs to the adapter that knows its hardware.</p> <p>Powermetrics NUL-framed plist parsing is lenient only for the final unparseable frame, and only after at least one complete frame parsed successfully. The adapter preserves the raw plist verbatim, drops that final frame only from derived parsing (<code>power_trace.csv</code> and rich telemetry), and records a non-gating <code>metadata.device.parse_diagnostics[]</code> entry describing the dropped tail. A midstream unparseable frame, or a capture with no complete frames, is still a hard parse failure.</p> <p>Mock telemetry sampling convention (D-019): for any nonzero <code>start_sampling</code>/<code>stop_sampling</code> span, <code>MockTelemetryAdapter</code> stamps synthetic measured samples strictly inside that adapter span, never at the boundary clock reads. It uses a centered nominal-period grid at the configured <code>sampling.power_hz</code>; if that would produce fewer than two samples, it emits two evenly spaced interior samples instead. This preserves deterministic constant-power math while ensuring the controller&#39;s post-start/pre-stop measured markers contain enough samples for reducer integration under both fake and real clocks.</p> <p>Initial telemetry backends:</p> <ul> <li><code>mock</code></li> <li><code>powermetrics</code></li> <li><code>nvidia_smi</code></li> <li><code>jetson_rails</code></li> <li><code>wall_meter</code></li> </ul> <h2 id="idle-admission-core-policy-extension-t0-5-audit-p1-1-p1-2-additive">Idle-Admission Core Policy Extension (T0.5, audit P1.1/P1.2; additive)</h2> <p>GPU-idle-only admission is no longer sufficient. The pure evaluators in <code>joulewise/idle_admission.py</code> add three fail-closed surfaces, driven by an additive campaign-policy sidecar section keyed <code>idle_admission_extension</code> (schema <code>joulewise.idle_admission_extension.v1</code>):</p> <ul> <li><p><strong>CPU-aware idle admission</strong>: policy-configurable criteria over the pre-run baseline rich telemetry (<code>rich_telemetry_idle.jsonl</code>) - nearest-rank p95 of the per-record max per-CPU busy ratio (<code>1 - idle_ratio - down_ratio</code>, clamped, so parked CPUs never read as busy) against <code>cpu_criteria.cpu_busy_ratio_p95_max</code>, and p95 of <code>processor_combined_power_w</code> against <code>cpu_criteria.processor_combined_power_w_p95_max</code>, with at least <code>cpu_criteria.min_samples</code> records. Admission requires the existing GPU-idle admission AND these criteria. Missing, malformed, or insufficient telemetry FAILS CLOSED when <code>cpu_criteria.on_missing_telemetry</code> is <code>fail</code> (mandatory for a production profile); an exploratory policy may use <code>flag</code> but must set <code>claim_bearing: false</code> (explicitly non-claim-bearing).</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Adapter-wattage continuity</strong>: <code>collect_environment_guard_observation</code> records the adapter surface (<code>power.adapter_watts</code>, <code>power.adapter_description</code>, plus a normalized <code>adapter_power_observation</code>) per admission observation when called with <code>include_adapter_power=True</code> (default off so pre-hookup callers keep their exact probe sequence AND their exact observation shape; the controller hookup opts in). Under the default flag the <code>power</code> block and <code>adapter_power_observation</code> keys are ABSENT entirely - not present as all-None placeholders - so the verdict&#39;s continuity scan (which treats any guard observation carrying a <code>power</code> key as an adapter observation) never ingests unverifiable unknown-wattage placeholders from callers that did not opt in. The campaign verdict evaluates the ordered observation sequence: wattage discontinuities (the live 140-&gt;70-&gt;140 W negotiation precedent) and description/power-source changes are NAMED conditions - recorded data, never a silent pass and never an implicit abort. Unknown adapter wattage fails closed when <code>adapter_wattage.require_known_wattage</code> is true (mandatory for production); stable known wattage passes.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Prospective NEG-8 SCREEN + BUDGET</strong> — <strong>Ed-ratified 2026-07-24, superseding the prior gross-only amendment:</strong> the screen is claim-family aligned. It independently gates gross and idle-subtracted point drift against distinct bounds derived from the same named, settled, same-condition <code>n &gt;= 10</code> corpus. The hash-sealed <code>joulewise.neg8_drift_bound.v1</code> artifact records both families. For legacy one-member endpoints, <code>d054_point_contrast_guard_v1</code> remains <code>max(sample_range_j, t_0.975,n-1 * s * sqrt(2))</code>. Prospective endpoints are three members each: the screen uses the start/end endpoint means, records their standard errors, and compares the absolute mean delta (not a second SEM-inflated margin) to <code>max(mean(largest_3)-mean(smallest_3), t_0.975,n-1 * s * sqrt(2/3))</code>. The extreme-triplet term retains the largest corpus-supported endpoint-mean contrast; the Student-t term predicts two new three-member endpoint means. Recording SEM without adding it again avoids double-counting repeatability already represented by the bound. Gross envelope corners remain diagnostics only.</p> <p>Every evaluated window also mints a strictly positive allowance per family: <code>max(max(start_mean,midpoint,end_mean)-min(...), derived_bound)</code>. One midpoint member is mandatory for the prospective 3+1+3 protocol, so a non-monotone interior excursion cannot disappear behind similar endpoints. No duration multiplier is applied: the settled corpus identifies repeatability, not a drift-per-time law, and inventing linear physics would be less defensible than the observed trajectory maximum. The verdict records the no-scaling decision, member counts/means/SEMs, midpoint, excursion, selected bound, allowance, and derivation hash. Floor records add the family-matched allowance after the guarded/corner-widened floor; validation recomputes the sum and claim consumption uses both the drift-widened floor and the named deterministic allowance term.</p> <p>Missing/invalid family evidence refuses distinctly: <code>neg8_drift_bound_underived</code> (gross) and <code>neg8_idle_sub_drift_bound_underived</code> (idle-subtracted); both spellings are Ed-ratified D-078 registry additions. Family failures retain <code>neg8_bracket_abs_delta_exceeded</code> for gross and add <code>neg8_bracket_idle_sub_abs_delta_exceeded</code> for idle-subtracted. A delta exactly on its bound passes. The v1 sidecar&#39;s <code>max_abs_delta_j</code>/<code>max_rel_delta</code> remain legacy transport fields and do not gate amended rows.</p> <p><strong>BOUND FRESHNESS addendum — Ed-ratified 2026-07-24:</strong> the same sealed artifact carries <code>freshness.derived_at_s</code>, a fixed 24-hour <code>max_age_s = 86400</code>, and exact OS-build, power-supply-identity, and calibration-artifact-identity bindings. Twenty-four hours mirrors the governed instrument-calibration horizon: it permits one controlled measurement day without treating repeatability as indefinitely transferable. Evaluation records its timestamp, expiry, artifact and observed bindings, binding-resolution status, and every triggered re-derivation reason. Horizon expiry, OS build change, power-supply change, calibration identity change, or unresolved current binding makes both family bounds stale and refuses with the registered <code>neg8_drift_bound_stale</code>. A v1 artifact with an authentic pre-addendum seal but no freshness block is replay-readable only to produce that stale refusal; it is never grandfathered. Malformed or unsealed artifacts remain underived under the two family-specific spellings. The superseded pre-SCREEN+BUDGET gross-only v1 shape (no <code>claim_family_bounds</code>) is not replayable and refuses as malformed/underived; &quot;pre-addendum replay&quot; applies only to the dual-family shape with <code>claim_family_bounds</code> present and freshness absent.</p> <p>The bracket is a WHOLE-WINDOW check: the evaluated basis must contain both endpoints. Legacy pair-only windows (a5-a8) remain evaluable as 1+0+1: both families screen and each allowance is <code>max(abs(delta), bound)</code>. Replicated endpoints plus midpoint apply prospectively; existing basis-scoped legacy verdict rows retain their frozen interpretation. Per-segment invocations with only one endpoint (or neither) record <code>neg8_bracket_not_evaluated</code>, never a spurious missing/failure. A reference genuinely absent from an explicit whole-window pass still fails closed.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Verdict surface: <code>scripts/run_campaign.py</code> records the additive <code>idle_admission_core</code> section (schema <code>joulewise.idle_admission_core_verdict.v1</code>) on the campaign verdict with per-member CPU-admission results, the continuity result, the bracket result, and the union of named conditions. A sidecar without the extension yields the named condition <code>idle_admission_extension_unconfigured</code>.</p> <p>Hash/version enforcement: the campaign policy binding hash is the sha256 of the full sidecar bytes, extension included - changing any new field changes the policy identity; the extension additionally records its own canonical-JSON sha256 and requires exact schema/policy version strings and exact keys (unknown or missing keys are rejected).</p> <p>Deployment note (C2 hookup complete): <code>CampaignPolicy.from_mapping</code> now owns the typed additive extension parse, including profile-dependent fail-closed validation, so controller child runs re-parse the full hash-bound sidecar without a runner-side strip/parse workaround. The tracked production and exploratory sidecars carry the extension. During each live admission attempt, the powermetrics adapter exposes that attempt&#39;s rich CPU records in memory; the controller evaluates CPU/combined-power criteria before workload invoke, records the result in the existing <code>environment_admission.attempts</code> ledger, and retries/aborts or flags according to the base policy. Attempt selection is explicit, so the final admission decision and final CPU telemetry cannot be paired across retries. Current-mint attempt rows bind each measurement to a finite <code>start_s</code>/<code>end_s</code> wall-clock (epoch) window; the ordered ledger must be strictly increasing and non-overlapping (<code>end_i &lt;= start_(i+1)</code>). Missing or malformed timing refuses current claims, while frozen replay semantics remain unchanged. Because the windows are wall-clock, a backwards clock step between attempts mints an out-of-order ledger that strict validation permanently refuses — a fail-closed false refusal, never an admission; re-run the campaign member if this occurs. Missing adapter telemetry fails closed on live clocks; <code>FakeClock</code> fixture runs retain the pre-hookup GPU decision and record <code>cpu_admission_enforced: false</code> alongside the named missing-telemetry result. That field is an unconditional claim barrier in reducers/extraction; it is never evidence that GPU-only admission was scientifically sufficient. Live guard observations opt in to adapter-power capture, including a mandatory post-workload observation for every member. A missing post sample is unknown wattage (and therefore a production refusal), so renegotiation during the final workload cannot be hidden by an earlier clean sample.</p> <p>At window end, chain scripts can run:</p> <pre><code class="language-sh">python3 scripts/run_campaign.py --whole-window-verdict \

Consequences verified: a\n6297\t   ~11.58 ms drift branch is budgetable; a 15 ms bracket refuses.\n6298\t   **Window B itself remains refused regardless** — its pre-calibration\n6299\t   0.035435840879704805 s (verified in primary evidence) exceeds the\n6300\t   pre-flight level screen, and D-079 cl.2's systematic failure is\n6301\t   never budgetable. The CAL-BRACKET regression at ~11 ms models the\n6302\t   DRIFT BRANCH only, never a whole-window B pass.\n6303\t2. **Freshness = exact identity epoch, no calendar hard expiry:** the\n6304\t   artifact binds {os_build, hardware_model, power_policy,\n6305\t   sampling_interval_ms, estimator_revision, pulse_protocol_id}; any\n6306\t   change → `calibration_acceptance_bound_stale`.
